item.title: Packers battling penalty onslaught
item.description: There’s little the Packers or NFL can do to fix the penalty situation.
item.content:encoded:
I’m of two minds when it comes to talking about the refs and penalties and everything that goes into officiating a professional football game.

On the one hand, officiating an NFL game is a massively complex undertaking. Have you read the NFL rulebook? Have you tried? A page turner it is not. The section for roughing the passer alone is 950 words. I know this for a fact because I checked after Sunday night’s impromptu roughing the passer festival, and now I’m actually surprised it isn’t called more considering the broad leeway officials have. It’s genuinely hard to know what to call and what not to call.

But on the other hand, shouldn’t it be…I don’t know…better than this? Every game is a flag fest and every play takes place under a looming yellow specter. Did a cool thing just happen? Better hold your breath until you see whether or not there’s laundry on the field. You never know when the capricious gaze of black-and-white striped justice will turn your way.

I know there’s plenty of data out there about the increase of penalties, but if you’ll allow me to get a little more squishy about it than just looking at the numbers, it feels bad out there. The vibe, as they say, is off. There’s little reason to assume any game you watch is going to unfold without at least one or two completely arbitrary penalties. Discussing any game inevitably hinges on what penalties were or were not called. It’s not a fun way to watch a game!

And I don’t know how you fix it. The genie is out of the bottle, in a sense, because you can’t just go back to not throwing as many flags. We’ve already seen what draws a penalty and what doesn’t. Walking it back now is just setting a different paradigm. That might be the only way, though. If nothing’s getting called, everything could feel less arbitrary. That’s small comfort in an NFL landscape increasingly ruled by seemingly random flags.

Unfortunately, Jeanty struggled with efficiency once again, managing just 22 yards on 10 carries, while adding another 36 yards on four receptions. A touchdown saved his fantasy day, but he was held under 60% of the snaps for the second straight week. 

Meanwhile, Washington played a season-high 35% of the snaps and turned his 10 touches into 50 scrimmage yards. That was aided by Jeanty getting only limited playing time in the second half, which was strange considering the game was tied 13-13 at halftime. 

Despite their claims of Jeanty's health last week, it doesn't seem like the 22-year-old is playing at 100%. It's unclear if the team will consider resting him, the same way the Cardinals did with Jeremiyah Love in Week 6, but it's a possibility.

Whenever a first-round wideout is immediately productive, fantasy managers should take notice. Mitchell is still week-to-week after undergoing surgery on his finger. Even when he returns, it's impossible to push Cooper aside based on what he's put on tape so far.

item.title: NFL Week 6 betting: 5 biggest storylines, including how Rams upset loss shook up the odds
item.description: The Rams lost to the Cardinals, and it had a ripple effect in the betting market.
item.content:encoded:
The biggest upset of the NFL season, in terms of point spread, came in Week 6.

The Los Angeles Rams lost straight up as 12.5-point favorites to the Arizona Cardinals. It's just the third time a favorite of 12.5 points or more has lost since the start of the 2023 season. The other two times came when the Titans beat the Dolphins, who were 13.5 point favorites, during the 2023 season and when the Packers lost as 13-point favorites to the Panthers last season. The Rams' loss had major ramifications across the odds, not just for the upcoming week but in the Super Bowl market.

Here are the betting storylines for Week 7 of the NFL season:

Rams-Raiders line shifts

There is a lot less confidence in the Rams after the loss to the Cardinals.

The Rams are just 4.5-point favorites at the Las Vegas Raiders for Week 7. The lookahead line last week, before Week 6 kicked off, was Rams -7, according to 4for4.com. Injuries to receiver Davante Adams and defensive lineman Kobie Turner also affected the line, but those injuries wouldn't normally move a point spread 2.5 points. And while the Raiders had a backdoor cover against the Bills on Sunday, their performance isn't why the line moved either.

It's just getting harder to trust the 2-4 Rams after Sunday.

New Super Bowl odds

The Rams were 2-3 last week but were still either favored to win the Super Bowl or their odds were tied with the Bills for the top spot. Finally, that has changed.

The Rams moved down to fifth in the Super Bowl odds. Here are BetMGM's odds after Week 6:

49ers +550

Bills +700

Chiefs +800

Ravens +1000

Rams +1200

While it's still odd to see a 2-4 team with the fifth-best Super Bowl odds, it's still a significant shift from +700 last week.

Chargers still haven't covered

The Chargers are a stunning 0-6 this season, and they hold a dubious dishonor as the final team in the NFL that hasn't covered the spread.

They're either 0-6 ATS or 0-5-1, depending on if their Week 4 loss to the Seahawks was scored as a push or a half-point loss.

The Los Angeles Chargers remain only NFL team still winless against the spread this season (0-5-1 ATS or 0-6 ATS, depending on Seattle Week 4 number)

— Ben Fawkes (@BFawkes22) October 18, 2026

The Chargers have a bye, but it's not like it will get much better for them considering some of their injury issues and overall poor play. But covering the spread soon shouldn't be too much to ask. Their first game after the bye? It's against the reeling Rams.

An early two-man race for MVP?

Josh Allen and Brock Purdy are distancing themselves in the MVP odds. After Purdy's impressive performance on Monday night and Allen helping the Bills to a win over the Raiders, they were atop the MVP odds board. Allen was +190 to win and Purdy was right behind at +225. Patrick Mahomes was well back of them at +900 and nobody else was +1100. For all the chatter that perhaps Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III should be included in the MVP conversation, he's still way back at 80-to-1. That's tied for 15th on the list, and 13 of the 14 players ahead of Walker are quarterbacks (Jahmyr Gibbs, at 66-to-1, is the only non-quarterback ahead of Walker).

There are many weeks for other quarterbacks to get in the MVP race. But after six weeks, everyone is chasing Allen and Purdy.

Chiefs are underdogs

The Chiefs' 5-0 start has been a bit overlooked, at least in terms of the buzz you'd expect from a Kansas City team being one of three remaining undefeated teams in the NFL. The Chiefs aren't even favored against a 3-3 team for Week 7.

It's not your typical .500 team, of course. The Chiefs play at the Seahawks next Sunday night. Seattle is -2.5 against Kansas City. The Seahawks offense has had its issues, including Sam Darnold's interceptions, but the defense is still excellent. It will be a good test for the Chiefs. If they win that, the buzz on them should increase.

Linebacker Jihad Ward's second stint with the Giants has come to a quick end.

According to multiple reports, the Giants have released Ward on Tuesday morning. Ward was signed off of the Vikings' practice squad in late September.

Ward played 41 defensive snaps and four special teams snaps in his two appearances with the team. He was credited with one tackle.

Ward also played in 34 games for the Giants during the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He moved on to the Vikings in 2024 and played for the Titans in 2025 before returning to Minnesota at the start of this season.

item.title: NFL Panic Meter: Is Brian Schottenheimer already in trouble for the Cowboys?
item.description: The Cowboys offense has fallen into a slump, and that's not good for the head coach.
item.content:encoded:
Jerry Jones isn't the type of impulsive owner everyone thinks he is, when it comes to firing head coaches.

The Dallas Cowboys have been too loyal over the past decade-plus. They have had three coaches since 2010, when Jason Garrett replaced Wade Phillips after a 45-7 loss to the Packers that dropped Dallas to 1-7. None of Dallas' three most recent coaches have taken the Cowboys to the NFC championship game. Despite that, Jones was patient with Garrett and then Mike McCarthy.

That doesn't mean he will have endless patience with Brian Schottenheimer.

The Cowboys came into the season talking about making a Super Bowl and they're 2-4. Dak Prescott talked about Dallas having "the greatest offense there is" and they've scored 29 points total the past two games. Jones himself led the talk about making a Super Bowl.

"I feel like we've got a chance to really be good," Jones said in late July at the beginning of training camp, via the Cowboys' site. "It's going to be hard. … Bottom line is, I love the excitement. [The media], for all practical purposes, don't expect us to be a contender in the Super Bowl. Y'all don't. Why would you? I like that, I do. I like that, and I like what we've put together to show you that we can do it."

When the owner, who just turned 84 years old, speaks like that and the team looks just as bad as it did last season when it went 7-9-1, then nobody should feel great.

To this point, the Cowboys are maintaining full support of Schottenheimer.

"Absolutely. There's not any question in Jerry's and [my] mind," Cowboys COO Stephen Jones, Jerry's son, told 105.3 The Fan. "He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen.

"Feel really good as I've mentioned throughout this conversation about our coaching staff. We just have to continue to have it evolve and get to a point where we can win these football games."

That's great to say, and Jerry Jones' recent history of patience has to be noted too. But now with the Cowboys' offense now in a slump — Dallas looked entirely unprepared to handle the Packers' blitzes and that's a reflection on Schottenheimer, who calls offensive plays — and the defense showing few signs of improvement, the season could go south quickly.

Jones is sticking with Schottenheimer. Dallas can turn it around, considering the next three games are against losing teams: at Eagles, vs. Cardinals, at Colts. If it doesn't look better over that stretch, we'll see if the mood at The Star changes.

Panic meter: There's always chaos in Dallas, but a 2-4 start is a real reason for concern. And Schottenheimer is really going to test Jones' patience if these next three games go poorly.

Bo Nix's struggles continue

It seems possible that Nix shows up in this space regularly through the season because the Denver Broncos offense isn't getting any better, even after head coach Sean Payton took over play-calling. The offense was particularly odorous on Thursday night against Seattle, when it had 38 offensive yards in the second half and overtime. Sam Darnold's interception in overtime bailed Denver out, and kept a little bit of attention off Nix, who was worse in his second season than he was as a rookie, and has been worse in his third season than he was last year.

Nix's microscopic 4.9-yard average depth of target is as bad as it gets, as CBS's Doug Clawson pointed out, and the sign of a quarterback with no confidence.

There are 701 qualified QB seasons through 6 games in the past 20 years

2026 Bo Nix ranks 701st out of 701 in average pass length (4.9 air yards per attempt)

His avg pass was thrown behind the line of scrimmage in the 2nd half on Thursday

— Doug Clawson (@doug_clawson) October 16, 2026

The Broncos have played a very tough schedule and perhaps that is the main reason Nix and Denver's offense has looked bad. But the schedule is lightening up, starting this week against Arizona, and Nix needs to look better.

Panic meter: We're probably one more bad game this week from a long and difficult conversation about the Broncos' quarterback situation.

How bad is the Davante Adams injury for Rams?

Davante Adams' injury on Sunday didn't look great, but it also didn't seem like it could ruin most of the rest of his season.

Adams is out 6-10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring. Other than losing Matthew Stafford, the Rams having one of their top two receivers go down was a worst-case injury scenario. One clear issue with the roster was the lack of depth at wide receiver after Adams and Puka Nacua (and was a reason everyone questioned taking quarterback Ty Simpson in the first round). The Rams might have to trade for a receiver to patch it through until Adams can return. It's a bad injury for a team that's off to a brutal 2-4 start.

Panic meter: The Rams season isn't dead but the offense is going to take a big step back without Adams.

Tanner McKee doesn't play well

There was a time when McKee was a hot name, based on some good preseason games. There was a thought that the Eagles could trade him for a huge haul, or even that he was a better option at quarterback than Jalen Hurts. After Sunday's start, that looks silly.

McKee, who was demoted to third string behind Andy Dalton before the season, struggled in his first start replacing Hurts. He had 215 yards on 45 attempts. The Eagles scored 14 points and never looked like a threat to beat the Panthers.

Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season and there's no magic solution for the Eagles. A 2-4 team shouldn't trade a ton for a quarterback, especially because any quarterback available in mid-October likely isn't that good. Teams don't like trading good backup quarterbacks. This is just what it is for the Eagles the rest of the season. It might not be pretty.

Panic meter: It's hard to say the Eagles' season is over already … but that's probably the answer.

Shane Steichen survives Colts purge, for now

There wasn't much surprise that a major move was made after the Colts lost to the winless Titans at home. The only surprise might have been that Steichen survived while general manager Chris Ballard was fired.

Part of the reason might be that nobody on the Colts staff has NFL head coaching experience. Some teams don't like changing head coaches in midseason because it can lead to chaos, especially if there's nobody experienced to take the job on an interim basis. But the Colts are the franchise that hired Jeff Saturday to be head coach in midseason even though he'd only coached in high school before then. They could have figured it out.

Steichen's Colts are 2-4, he had never led the team to the playoffs and owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has spoken often about the urgency the franchise has this season. She acted on that by firing Ballard. At this point, it seems like anything short of the Colts rallying for a playoff spot could cost Steichen his job. And that will be especially difficult if the Colts start selling before the trade deadline.

Panic meter: It's looking pretty hopeless in Indianapolis, especially for Steichen.

Will J.J. McCarthy make the Vikings look bad?

The Minnesota Vikings didn't get much back when they traded McCarthy. They sent the 10th pick of the 2024 NFL Draft to the Giants for a fifth-round pick a few weeks ago. On Sunday, McCarthy came in for the Giants in the fourth quarter and had 243 passing yards in 11 minutes. The Vikings haven't thrown for 243 yards in a game yet this season.

Is it possible that the Vikings will look very foolish for selling so low on McCarthy after 10 career starts? Possibly. But one good quarter, when the Giants got hot after falling behind by 24 points, is far from proof that McCarthy is an emerging star and was just held back in Minnesota. But still, it's at least possible that this ends up as a regrettable, impatient trade for the Vikings.

Panic meter: Let's see it from McCarthy again before we revisit the trade.

item.title: NFL Power Rankings Week 7 Roundup: Chiefs settle into No. 2 spot
item.description: Let’s see where Kansas City is ranked for Week 7 of the NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 NFL regular season’s Week 6 featured the Kansas City Chiefs beating the Los Angeles Chargers to push their unbeaten record to 5-0.

Let’s see how the national media tweaked their opinion on the Chiefs over the weekend in this week’s sampling of power rankings:

ESPN: 2

(No change)

Biggest issue on offense: Offensive tackle health

The Chiefs have done an admirable job protecting quarterback Patrick Mahomes, especially since left tackle Josh Simmons, their 2025 first-round pick, has been out because of a bulging disc in his lower back. Coach Andy Reid suggested Simmons won’t be ready for Sunday’s showdown against the Seahawks. Plus, right tackle Jaylon Moore sustained a concussion against the Chargers. Reid might have to continue altering the Chiefs’ playbook if undrafted rookies Kahlil Benson (left tackle) and Joshua Ezeudu (right tackle) are the starters.

— Nate Taylor

The Athletic: 2

(No change)

Fantasy focus: Kenneth Walker III

The Chiefs won six games last year. They signed Walker to a three-year, $43 million deal in the offseason. On Sunday, they won their fifth game. Walker is second in the league in fantasy points per game (27.6) after being drafted 16th on average. He had 19 carries for 128 yards against the Chargers and leads the league with 665 rushing yards.

— Chad Graff and Josh Kendall

Pro Football Talk: 2

(No change)

Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III is the NFL MVP so far.

— Mike Florio

CBSSports.com: 2

(No change)

Coming out of the bye, they dominated the Chargers. The same formula worked: Run it with Kenneth Walker and timely throws by Patrick Mahomes, who is doing more and more each week.

— Pete Prisco

Yahoo! Sports: 2

(No change)

It’s hard to believe that an offense with Patrick Mahomes at quarterback has been turned over to another player, but Kenneth Walker III’s impact on the Chiefs can’t be understated. Walker had another 128 yards and two touchdowns on the ground as the Chiefs easily beat the Chargers 22-6. Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, even though Kansas City has already had its bye. His 133 rushing yards per game puts him on pace for 2,261 rushing yards. Since 1984, Eric Dickerson has held the NFL’s single-season record with 2,105 yards.

Walker’s candidacy for MVP will be discussed, but it’s still a long shot because voters have turned it into a quarterback award. Adrian Peterson was the last non-quarterback to win and that came in 2012. The MVP has gone to a quarterback 18 of the last 19 seasons. But if Walker can get to 2,000 yards, it might give him a chance.

— Frank Schwab

USA Today: 2

(No change)

Andy Reid is now 23-5 in the regular season following bye weeks. Sure looks like he might get the opportunity to coach after another bye a few months from now.

— Nate Davis

Sports Illustrated: 2

(Up from 3)

Asking this seriously: Kenneth Walker is the best free agent signing through six weeks of an NFL season since…Peyton Manning and the Denver Broncos? Walker is averaging one hundred and thirty three yards and more than twenty attempts per game. That’s just wild stuff.

— Conor Orr

Sporting News: 1

(No change)

Kenneth Walker III is now averaging 133 rushing yards per game and is up to 6.3 yards per carry with his 8 TDs. He’s on pace 2,261 yards, which should already put him in the MVP discussion as one of the best-ever free-agent pickups.

— Vinnie Iyer

FOX Sports: 2

(No change)

Is it possible that the Chiefs are actually under the radar for most of the NFL? Or maybe we just all take their greatness for granted? But there sure isn’t a lot of chatter or hype about what might be the best team in the league. And Patrick Mahomes, just 10 months removed from tearing his ACL, is quietly on pace for his best season since 2022 — when he won league MVP and the Chiefs won the Super Bowl. Maybe Mahomes belongs in the early MVP conversation, too? The Chiefs play at Seattle and at Denver these next two weeks, so the noise about K.C. is about to get a lot louder.

— Ralph Vacchiano

item.title: Why the Seahawks don’t need to bench Sam Darnold
item.description: Why benching Sam Darnold isn’t necessarily the answer, at this point
item.content:encoded:
We’ve all sat with this one for a bit. Is Sam Darnold not the answer? Did he get rushed back from injury? Would the Seahawks be better off with Andrew Lock as the trigger man?

One thing is clear: Seven interceptions in four games is… not good. Pulling the struggling quarterback can feel like the quickest and easiest lever to pull.

The Seattle Seahawks, of course, will have a long wait until they can wash the sour taste of recent putrid performances on offense out of their collective mouths. The run of losses to the San Francisco 49ers and the Denver Broncos in the last two games featured plenty of frustrating mistakes to pave the road to an unspectacular 3-3 record. How do the 2026 Seahawks continue to run it forward?

Brock Purdy hadn’t been sacked before facing the ‘Hawks, then got taken down three times by the “Dark Side.” That stop unit held SF to 4/12 on 3rd downs and tainted his pristine trajectory to hand him his 2nd INT of the season (first since the opening week). Bo Nix was held under 110 passing yards. It’s the offense that failed in their mission to be complimentary.

Does Seattle need to bench their championship quarterback? Let’s start by not turning the ball over.

I want to preface all of this and say that backup halfback, George Holani was questionable to play in Santa Clara. With that in mind, he deserves some appropriate credit, as a warrior for this team. He also deserves credit for being a strong pass protector… at times.

Having said that, the man put the ball on the ground twice against the Niners, contributing to a sloppy performance by the Hawks. If you did not know, NFL coaches are serious about fumbles. That hyperlink is the Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady talking about reducing the load of player who led the league in rushing TD’s in 2024 and rushing yards in 2025.

The thing is, Holani averages over seven touches per game. Before TNF, Shaheed was averaging a little over two touches per. I know you don’t want to have tells when a specific back is in the game… but perhaps time for less?

That’s what I thought before the Broncos game. Rashid Shaheed got $34M guaranteed on his contract extension this past offseason. I wanted to see the Hawks use short passes as an extension of the run game, if need be, just to get his involvement in line with his contract priority.

Then that man fumbled twice.

Who’s next to get added to the mix? Here are Tory Horton’s last 8 catches: first down, touchdown, 6 yards, touchdown, first down, first down, first down, touchdown. He was not targeted in Week 6 against the Niners. Tory, come on down!!

Interceptions are a little more convoluted of a blame game than fumbles. Cooper Kupp addressed the throw to Horton: “certainly within the grounds of what that play was. Got to make a play.” The same Cooper who is no longer a dynamic threat on the field.

Is it possible that the 2026 Seattle Seahawks are simply in need of another high-level playmaker to join JSN in the priority list for defenses to worry about? Kenneth Walker III was that last season, but I’m not sure he’s the only. Is the pantry now raided? Does Seattle need to draft a wideout in the first round in the upcoming offseason? Let’s hit pause on that for now.

Is it the offensive line? I mean, Abe Lucas’ performance was groan-worthy at times. When discussing the five sacks that Darnold took and how it reflects on the offensive line, Mike Macdonald explained, saying, “I mean, you can say it’s on the offensive line–it’s on our offense. You know, it’s both. It’s how efficient we can run the ball; how efficient we can move the ball other ways. The quarterback is getting hit way too much, so everybody sees that.”

There are multiple angles here. Role players may be touching the ball a little more than originally planned, but also there is the question of scheme. As Field Gulls’ own Mookie Alexander mentions, “At the moment, the Seahawks do not have the type of offense that can control a game through the run. They are a much better passing team on early downs yet adopt a run-first mentality.”

Mike Macdoanld on why the ball is being put in jeopardy so often: “In short, it’s really a function of ‘who’s applying pressure to who?’ So, if we’re playing the way we want to play, we should be applying pressure to defenses. Then, all of a sudden –it’s funny how that works–ball isn’t as in jeopardy as much.”

It’s unfortunate that the running back that the ‘Hawks took in Round 1 of the NFL draft joins another early round back on the injury ledger, in Zach Charbonnet. Those two, along with up-and-comers like Jacardia Wright and (the no longer on the roster) Kenny McIntosh all being unavailable is sad. Does that mean that we should hit the panic button?

Darnold does need to get into flow state. And yes: Sam should be expected to be able to get it done… even in the absence of a run game. Even if conditions are not perfect, we should expect him to be able to figure it out. He’s a Super Bowl-winning signal caller, but if he keeps throwing two INT’s per game, Seattle brass may have to pull him at some point. That point is not now.

Coach Mike addressed the controversy around Sam Darnold, saying that, “I know we’re harping on the turnovers… but he’s been able to escape some really nasty pressure situations and find ways to move the ball down the field, that not a lot of people can do. That’s definitely in his skillset and we encourage him to continue to do that, within your progressions and things like that.”

Seattle prides itself on cultivating environments for passers to succeed in. That environment seems crippled at the moment.

Macdonald plainly stated that, “we got to be able to execute our run game and hold on to the football… straight up.” All of the coaches on staff will be tasked with exploring ways to improve this slumping offense.

Those of you who think Brian Fleury and, to some extent, Sam Darnold are under some level of pressure are kidding yourselves. There is a standard. It will be interesting to see what Fleury chooses to change, if anything, headed into a possible humiliation ritual against Ken Walker.

Now, acknowledging that things need to change, we can also understand that making a QB change is a very big deal. It’s one that has ripple effects on the direction of the franchise for years to come.

We can blame the run game, we can blame injuries, we can blame Shaheed, we can blame Tory Horton, we can blame the offensive line, and yes… we can blame Sam Darnold. Hell, you can blame Hard Knocks if you want to. This is not the end of the season as we know it.

The Seahawks have totaled 10 turnovers in their 3 losses… and still only lost those by a collective sum of 8 points overall. Maybe the sky isn’t truly falling quite yet. Let’s just wait and see what things look like when Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet and Anthony Bradford make their returns to the lineup.

Yes, THAT Anthony Bradford.

item.title: Eagles News: Jalen Hurts situation “shakes the foundation of what we think we know about how the team operates”
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 10/20/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

As the great Zach Berman has said, people will speculate in the absence of information. And the Eagles might not enjoy that speculation. But if the Eagles have permission from Jalen Hurts to share more about the specifics of his situation, it sure seems like they should.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Bowen: We still don’t know enough about Jalen Hurts’ situation, but we know the Eagles organization is reeling & looks incompetent – PHLY Eagles

It’s irritating when coaches do this, because they know very well the medical staff is not available to answer anything. As one Sirianni questioner pointed out, Sirianni is the team spokesman here. It would be reasonable to expect him to be briefed by the medical staff before going out to answer questions. In fact, this was an occasion on which we might have expected to hear from Howie Roseman or even Jeffrey Lurie. Instead we got Sirianni repeating himself, starting multiple answers with “again,” as if all of this was just so repetitive and tiresome for him, hours after we learned the extent of the problem. “We put out a detailed statement for you guys to hear and to understand,” Sirianni said. The only thing Sirianni really made clear is that it wasn’t his decision, to play Hurts or to fly him home. He might get fired this season because of losing, but from what we know right now, I wouldn’t expect this matter to directly lead to Sirianni’s departure. (It could certainly do so indirectly, by exacerbating the losing.) Someone, maybe multiple someones on the team’s medical staff surely will have to have to answer for this, though. […] But it’s bad enough to cast doubt on Hurts’ future here, and by extension, on Sirianni’s future. The organization hasn’t been at a crossroads like this since Carson Wentz demanded to be traded. Even then, though, the Eagles had Hurts. I don’t see Tanner McKee taking the team to any Super Bowls. Overall, this is a shocking failure from an organization that prides itself on its professional standards. It shakes the foundation of what we think we know about how the team operates.

Is there a trust issue between Jalen Hurts and the Eagles? – BGN

One thing is for certain, some close to Hurts were not happy with how the Eagles dealt with the blood clot situation. They also felt Hurts should have been treated far better by the team this offseason by offering another contract extension. The Eagles never budged. With the perception of how the Eagles dealt with Hurts’ situation, coupled with the looming contract extension, it may not help the relationship.

The Eagles Somehow Made the Jalen Hurts Situation Even Worse on Monday – SI

This is purely my opinion: I am not sure what the Eagles would have ultimately gained by sneaking Hurts onto the field knowing he was suffering through a dire medical condition and then parking the franchise quarterback on an airplane to let the condition worsen. Again, doing this knowingly would be one of the most significant medical controversies in NFL history and would require firing an entire medical staff. As Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk noted, demand a reexamination of everything when it comes to the way we treat players. Certainly, there have been high-profile stories of team medical professionals acting negligently, and I am not naive to the fact that a doctor can make a horrible mistake. However, this would represent a multiperson, department-wide breakdown for which I don’t have a reference point. But if this were the case, wouldn’t Hurts’s agent be publicly warring against the Eagles on behalf of her client instead of collaborating on a statement with them? There are so many details about the nuances of the treatment, what was known at the time in London, what kind of testing equipment was available to the Eagles in another country before the team made a decision to play Hurts, and what, ultimately, was passed along to the person or people deciding it was O.K. for Hurts to play. We cannot have this narrative both ways: The Eagles seemed to be preparing for a rebuild and, weeks ago, traded one of their best remaining offensive linemen after the Johnson retirement. They also needed to win a game in the absolute destitute swampland that is the NFC East so badly that they would put a quarterback in a life-threatening situation?

The Biggest Questions About Jalen Hurts’s Health, and Where the Eagles Go From Here – The Ringer

What does this mean for Hurts’s future with the Eagles? Hurts was likely going to be one of the main characters of the 2027 offseason even before this blood clot issue. He’s under contract through 2028, but the bulk of the guaranteed money from the deal he signed in 2023 has already been paid out, and the team could get out of his contract after next season for just a $54.5 million dead cap hit. It’s also possible that Hurts could have been a trade candidate next spring, if the Eagles were interested in moving on, or, if this season had gone well, they might have considered extending him early, before the QB market explodes. Lamar Jackson, C.J. Stroud, and Bryce Young will be among the passers looking for new deals next offseason, just as the quarterbacks from the 2024 draft class—including Caleb Williams and Drake Maye—become eligible for second contracts. The Eagles often try to be ahead of the market—that was the case in 2023 when they got Hurts’s last extension done before Jackson’s new deal with Baltimore. Now, though, it’s not simply a question of timing or cost to keep Hurts, but Philadelphia needing to decide if he’s even still their long-term quarterback. The Eagles are currently on their third offensive coordinator/play caller in the last three years; the most recent change, from Kevin Patullo to Sean Mannion, a Matt LaFleur protege, brought an entirely new scheme for Hurts, one with increased time under center and more frequent use of play-action. The early results haven’t been great—though the injuries, particularly Barkley’s, and personnel changes along the offensive line have made it difficult to give the system a true evaluation. Siranni signed a contract extension in 2025 within months of the Eagles’ most recent Super Bowl title, but it’s hard to imagine that his job is super secure as yet another season spirals away. Playing the rest of this year without Hurts just makes all of those offseason questions more difficult to answer.

Eagles QB Jalen Hurts’ blood clot diagnosis explained – ESPN

Hurts was originally diagnosed with having a superficial blood clot, according to a team statement released on Oct. 15, which was discovered following an ultrasound in London before the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It was deemed that mobility was important and Hurts could safely play in the game, per the statement. A follow-up ultrasound last Wednesday showed the blood clot had moved, the team said. Hurts was subsequently ruled out of Sunday’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers and has since been put on injured reserve. ESPN spoke with Dr. Jordan K. Schaefer, associate professor of internal medicine at the University of Michigan specializing in disorders of hemostasis and thrombosis, for a better understanding of causes, treatments, and outlook for those with blood clots. Dr. Schaefer has not treated Hurts and is not involved with the Eagles. The conversation has been edited for brevity and clarity.

Jalen Hurts is out for the season. Where do the spiraling Eagles go from here? – The Athletic

The problem with this conversation? The worse the Eagles finish, the worse it is for Sirianni’s future with the organization. This might be a sensitive subject — and some might even call it unfair speculation — for a coach who has won a Super Bowl and has the best winning percentage among qualified active coaches. One losing season, with the franchise quarterback lost after Week 5, would seem like an acceptable mulligan. This is also where Lurie’s history is instructive. The focus has been on trajectory — not resume. After the 2020 season, Pederson was fired after his first post-Super Bowl losing season. Lurie said Pederson did not “deserve” to be dismissed, but the franchise made the move to set a new direction. If Pederson had returned in 2021, Lurie felt the coach would need to do everything possible to maximize that season. The Eagles knew they needed to build for beyond 2021. Lurie fired Chip Kelly in 2015 after his first losing season following two 10-win campaigns. The franchise’s direction was a concern. After the 2012 season, Lurie moved on from Andy Reid — the winningest coach in franchise history — when Reid needed a change of scenery and the Eagles needed a fresh voice.

Hurt Hurts Update – Iggles Blitz

If the Eagles stick with the young guys, that could be a sign they are embracing this as a lost season. If they add a veteran, that could signal they still want to try to win the division and make the playoffs. That may sound nuts in the middle of a 4-game losing streak, but the team could get a boost as some hurt players start returning from their injuries. Howie and Nick are the kind of guys who will want to compete as long as possible. A weird season seems to get weirder every week. If you’re an older fan this might remind you of 1993, 2005, 2012 or 2020. The Eagles expected to be really good in those years and then things went haywire. I might get PTSD if I start thinking too much about them. The biggest common denominator was injuries. That certainly is a huge issue for the current team.

NFL Week 6 Sunday aftermath: Texans surging after huge AFC South win; panic time for Rams? – NFL.com

The Eagles’ offense could be unsalvageable with Monday’s stunning news that Jalen Hurts will likely miss the rest of the season due to blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee looked like a preseason quarterback early on Sunday against Carolina. The NFL is played in millimeters; McKee missed by feet at times. He found a groove late by feeding DeVonta Smith, but if he regresses to who he was early in the tilt and struggles under pressure, the Eagles’ offense will continue to fly listless. In addition, the line issues offer little hope that the attack will turn things around this season. It will be interesting to see how Howie Roseman handles the next few weeks before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Does the Eagles general manager make a move for a veteran replacement at QB? Does Philly ride with McKee even if the backup struggles? Does 2026 become a reboot season, where the franchise ultimately just hopes to get everything back on track in 2027? After parting with Cam Jurgens to compile picks, shelling out for a stopgap QB could run counter to the stockpile plan. On the other hand, Roseman has to look at the rest of the division and feel like he still has a shot at winning it if he can get competent QB play.

The goal of team doctors shouldn’t be to help players “be available” – PFT

Here’s what Sirianni said, when asked to identify the persons who were part of the conversations surrounding the medical decisions made after a blood clot was discovered in Hurts’s leg: “I think I’ll put it this way, the same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys to help them.” (Emphasis added.) The doctors shouldn’t be there to help players “be available.” They should be there to provide medical care to players who, when they have a health issue, become patients. Without an unaffiliated doctor involved in the process, the objective easily can shift from taking the best care of the patient to best enhancing the ability of the player to play. That’s why the Hurts case should be the starting point for a comprehensive examination of the entire system of providing medical care to NFL players. With the player wanting to be able to play and the team wanting the player to be able to play, a doctor who is perceived as saying too often “this player shouldn’t be available to play” risks being replaced by a doctor who understands the unspoken (usually) goal of ensuring that as many players as possible will “be available” to play in every game.

Nick Sirianni: Eagles sticking with Sean Mannion as play-caller – NBCSP

After Sunday’s loss to the Panthers, head coach Nick Sirianni said “everything is on the table” to fix the Eagles’ stagnant offense. But he’s not changing play-callers. On Monday afternoon, Sirianni said he is sticking with first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion in that role. “Obviously, we are looking at everything,” Sirianni added a day after his team’s fourth consecutive loss. “Again, I think those are conversations that I’ve had with the staff this whole morning. Everything’s on the table. ‘Oh but we’ve done this.’ Well, maybe this isn’t working quite as good so this is on the table. Without getting too much into scheme-wise, I’m saying to you, obviously, it hasn’t looked the way we wanted it to look and we’re not scoring enough points. So everything is on the table. I’ll do everything we can do, our coaches will do everything we can do to help us win football game. If I said, ‘this is all on the table but this isn’t’ … everything’s on the table. But as far as who’s coaching the positions and who’s calling the plays, that will remain the same. We’re looking for answers and we’re looking for solutions.”

FOOTBALL COURT: Is Bryce Young is the NFL MVP so far? – SB Nation

This NFL season is completely off the rails in the best way possible. Nothing is predictable, all our assumptions have been torn asunder, and somehow we’re sitting at the end of Week 6 with there being very real, sensible discussions over whether Bryce Young is on pace to win the NFL MVP award. Young has become the league’s most-talked about quarterback (at least in a positive way). He’s absolutely balling out in year four, playing almost mistake-free football, with his only two interceptions being on final plays of the half or drive where they were chalked up as true desperation plays. Meanwhile he’s moving the ball vertically better than almost anyone in the league, and is on pace to finish with 5,267 yards, 37 TDs, and 7 INTs — all while cementing the Panthers as the best team in the NFC South, with everyone else lagging far behind.

CJ Gardner-Johnson suspended one game for spitting incident vs. Raiders – Buffalo Rumblings

To the surprise of no one, the NFL has levied a suspension on Buffalo Bills safety CJ Gardner-Johnson for spitting in the direction of Brock Bowers in the second quarter of the Week 6 game in Las Vegas.

Mike Evans and Kyle Juszczyk are active for the 49ers – Niners Nation

Wonder if the Eagles might look to bring one of their former blockers back to Philly. Brett Toth is a better option than Jake Majors.

The San Francisco 49ers released veteran offensive lineman Brett Toth from injured reserve as part of an injury settlement, per Matt Maiocco. That should tell us the team was not expecting Toth to return this season, while acknowledging they may play another player on the injured reserve.

Colts Working Out Two Receivers Including Ainias Smith – NFL Trade Rumors

Aaron Wilson of KPRC reports the Colts are hosting WRs Ainias Smith and Courtney Jackson for workouts on Monday. Smith, 25, declared for the draft after his fifth year at Texas A&M. He was drafted by the Eagles in the fifth round with the No. 152 overall pick of the 2024 NFL Draft.

Darian Kinnard: Headed to Las Vegas – CBS Sports

Former Eagles OL lands in Sin City.

Kinnard (ankle) was signed to the Raiders’ practice squad Monday. Kinnard was released by the Packers in late August after suffering an ankle injury.

NY Giants ‘working through’ quarterback decision, won’t make one yet – Big Blue View

New York Giants coach John Harbaugh said on Monday afternoon that the Giants have not yet made a decision who their starting starting quarterback will be on Sunday against the Houston Texans. “We’re working through that now. Honing in on a decision,” Harbaugh said via Zoom. The Giants, of course, have a decision to make after J.J. McCarthy threw for 243 yards and led the Giants from a34-10 deficit to the brink of a stunning comeback on Sunday in a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints. What will the decision be based on? “Absolutely like every other personnel decision we make what gives us the best chance to win the football game at this given time or what combination of players and schemes and things like that give us the best chance to, in this case, move the ball, score points, protect the football, etc.,” Harbaugh said. “The things that help us win. Whatever it is that furthers us and helps us. That’s what we want to do.”

Cowboys at Packers Stock Report: Brian Schottenheimer leads latest downward trend – Blogging The Boys

Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer — What is unique about this moment is that the Cowboys had the mini-bye to prepare for this game. Obviously the goal was to win, but if they had shown fight then at least you could make an argument that they were prepared and simply fell short. That was not the case. This team looks flat and like it lacks leadership, so the leadership is in serious question. […] Stock Down: Dak Prescott — This was certainly one of the worst games of Dak Prescott’s career. What happened to the version of Dak that excelled against the blitz? Maybe defenses have figured out a way to neutralize what he took advantage of, but right now it has seriously become the quarterback’s kryptonite. A lot went wrong. But the franchise quarterback being a part of that is never a good thing.

NFC Hierarchy/Obituary: Week 7 edition – PhillyVoice

10) Cowboys (2-4): The Cowboys lost 23-13 in Green Bay, but it wasn’t really even that close. Packers receivers dropped a bunch of touchdowns, and Dak Prescott laughably had an INT wiped off his stat sheet because of this extraordinarily soft roughing the passer flag. With the Eagles going through a “season from hell,” the division is right there for the Cowboys to take, and they’re basically like, “Nah.

Key takeaways from Washington Commanders loss to San Francisco 49ers – Hogs Haven

Proving that they were better and had rebounded well was a tough task, however, considering they had to fly across the country to play the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday night. The 49ers were more talented at most every spot, even with San Francisco beset by with injuries. Leaving with a win was always considered tough – it would’ve been huge considering the dismal state of the NFC East – but remaining competitive seemed necessary. Despite an awful first half, the Commanders certainly were. And wouldn’t ya know it, this game also came down to a last-second scenario, with the Commanders pushing to win the game with no timeouts and less than a minute left. Could the Commanders handle this late-game scenario? The game management wasn’t the issue here, but the result wasn’t any better. The game was in the balance, with the Commanders pushing hard for a score with less that an minute left. In the decisive play, Daniels was called for an intentional grounding call that generated a loss of down and a 10 second runoff, setting up a presumptive last-second chuck into the end zone.

Season of a lifetime begins as Sixers face defending champion Knicks– Liberty Ballers

We have arrived. The beginning of the most highly anticipated Sixers season of our lifetimes is upon us. A starting five of stars past, present, and future has been assembled to take Philadelphia to the promised land known as “beyond the second round of the playoffs”. It all still feels a bit surreal. The Jaylen Brown trade came out of nowhere, after we had all but resigned ourselves to a purgatory riding out the contracts of Paul George and Joel Embiid. Now every conversation about the team seems like a harpist is playing while a personal chef prepares our dinner. The possibility of LeBron James signing with the Sixers was certainly discussed. But surely he would return to a past home in Cleveland or Miami. It was nice just to be thrown into the mix. Now the always a bridesmaid is being rushed to the altar in a helicopter from New York.

item.title: NFC West Recap: 49ers continue to distance themselves; Rams and Seahawks lose
item.description: Two straight weeks of perfect football for 49ers fans. Makes you forget about the wackiness of the Commanders game.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers had another good week of football. Sure, their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders unnecessarily came down to the wire, but they still won. The best part is, everyone else lost! AGAIN!

The 49ers have beaten the Commanders—a team the Seattle Seahawks lost to. They have also beaten the Denver Broncos, a team both the Rams and Seahawks lost to. Should tiebreakers come into play, those two victories could be a deciding factor.

So that puts the 49ers at 6-0 and 3-0 in the division. With the losses, they now have a three-game lead (and change if you could tiebreakers) over the second-place Seahawks.

Yes, the Commanders win wasn’t pretty, but the 49ers are 6-0, and if we have to endure a game like that Commanders game to be 6-0, I don’t think there’s a fan in the world who wouldn’t take that.

It’s not without some wrinkles. Wide receiver Mike Evans may miss some time. While Christian Kirk has resumed practice, it might take some time to get in sync with Brock Purdy. At least the 49ers get Dre Greenlaw back next week and maybe Nick Bosa.

Seattle Seahawks (3-3)

The biggest thing about the Seahawks’ loss to the Denver Broncos isn’t that they lost a game they probably should have won; it’s that Bo Nix may be getting more criticism for his play than Sam Darnold.

And he should. Nix has had a tendency to come back in the second half in 2026, but he didn’t do any of that here. You can also add in some very bad decision-making. Nix went 17 for 27 and 107 yards passing. Yes, 107 yards passing and the Broncos won. It’s fair to note the Broncos also had 74 yards rushing.

So how did the Broncos win? Defense, all defense. How did the Seahawks lose? Well, not being able to run the ball might be the biggest reason. 113 yards total. Rashid Shaheed losing one of his two fumbles doesn’t help. Then there’s the other quarterback. Sam Darnold had two interceptions, zero touchdowns, and five sacks.

17-14, Broncos. The Broncos are 4-2 after that stat line from Bo Nix. He didn’t throw a touchdown or an interception and got sacked twice compared to Darnold’s five. Do the Broncos look like a 4-2 team? That’s up to you. The Seahawks are now games (yes, plural) behind the 49ers, and it’s not going to get any easier.

Arizona Cardinals (2-4)/Los Angeles Rams (2-4)

Oh, you know what time it is. Let’s Ram It! Let’s Ram it all the way to last place in the NFC West.

The Arizona Cardinals not only beat the Los Angeles Rams, but did so by field-goal-ing the Rams to death. Six field goals were all the Cardinals needed to get the 18-16 victory.

This was a Los Angeles Rams team that some thought would go undefeated before the season began. Now they are last place in their own division. My, what a tangled web we weave.

And the Rams had a chance to win this thing. They marched down the field, got the touchdown, and the Cardinals only had 45 seconds left with no timeouts. Turns out 45 seconds is too much time for Jacoby Brissett, because next thing you know he’s pushing the ball down the field and getting into field goal range in 10 of those 45 seconds.

Many are saying the Rams get an easier schedule so they can right the ship, but again: They lost to a team via six field goals. The only other team the Cardinals have beaten is from Los Angeles, and that team, the Chargers, is 0-6 right now.

And yes, the Rams lost their kicker early in the game and didn’t have a kicker to make field goals. Then again, should the Rams need a kicker for the Cardinals?

That’s a huge win for the Cardinals and an equally miserable loss for the Rams. Are they out? No. But they are now in last place with several divisional losses on them as well. They are almost at “run the table to get in the playoffs” territory. Almost.

And it gets worse. First, wide receiver Davante Adams is out 6-10 weeks due to a hamstring injury. That’s devastating for the wide receiver group (something 49ers fans know all too well). Second, their shiny new kicker, Blake Grupe, was injured on Sunday, which was enough to add him to injured reserve.

So the Rams need to overcome a four-game deficit without a kicker or their veteran wide receiver.

Onto Week 7

The 49ers will travel to face the Atlanta Falcons, a game with the dreaded 10:00 AM start time. Not exactly ideal when the Falcons have been humming for a couple of games until Sunday—when the Chicago Bears crushed them. That score says 31-23, but 16 of the Falcons’ 23 points came in the fourth quarter.

Meanwhile, Chicago was scoring touchdowns until the fourth quarter. Regardless of Atlanta’s performance, they have the best running back in the game in Bijan Robinson. With Robinson, the Falcons can run the ball, and if you’ve watched them lately, he’s not exactly the easiest thing to stop. It’s a great test for the 49ers, who have limited explosive runs.

The Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs as the Sunday Night Football game. It feels strange to want the Seahawks to win just to hand the Chiefs a loss, but the Chiefs could do the 49ers a favor by putting the Seahawks to 3-4. As much as some of us may dislike both teams, that will be a fun game to watch. Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will probably be the star of the show; the Seahawks running game hasn’t been the same since he left in free agency, and the Chiefs have had a running game since acquiring him.

The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos. The same Denver Broncos who managed to beat the Seahawks. Given what we’ve seen of this Cardinals team, a win isn’t out of the ordinary.

The Rams will have their second straight week of not playing on primetime. They might play a bit more on Sunday afternoon if the league flexes them out of anything in the future. They host the Las Vegas Raiders. The Raiders lost to the Buffalo Bills, but were in it until the end. The Rams could be their get-right game.

1st: San Francisco 49ers Next at Atlanta Falcons

2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: vs. Kansas City Chiefs (Sunday Night Football)

3rd: Arizona Cardinals; Next: vs. Denver Broncos

4th: Los Angeles Rams; Next: at Las Vegas Raiders

item.title: Detroit Lions bye week evaluation: Is the team really on the rise?
item.description: Should Detroit Lions fans really be more optimistic than in 2025?
item.content:encoded:
One of the more interesting comments from Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell on Monday was his level of optimism at the bye week compared to last year. Even though Detroit had come off a big win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to move to 5-2 last year, Campbell said he feels better about this season because of the youth and growth already shown through five games.

“In some regards I feel better going into this bye than even I did last year because I know we’re ascending and we’re young and we’re growing and that’s exciting,” Campbell said. “Sometimes you feel like you’re topped off and maybe you’re beginning to deteriorate because of issues worn down, age, whatever it is.

“So that’s exciting. I do feel like we’re on the rise here a little bit. We’ve just got to keep getting better. We’ve got to keep testing ourselves. And look, we’re in for the long haul now and it’s really about to get geared up and the competition is about to really raise up another level, and it starts with Green Bay.”

But is that optimism actually warranted? Is this team’s future far more bright than the one that finished 9-8 and out of the playoffs last year?

On this week’s PODcast, we re-evaluate how the team has played through five games. What have they done well? What have they struggled with? What successes are likely to continue through January, and which struggles could actually improve in the back half of the season?

Last year, John Morton led the highest-scoring offense in the league through the first couple months. What is different about this season that could keep the offense efficient throughout the entire year? And what hope is there that the Lions defense can turn things around?

In the last portion of the PODcast, we discuss the outlook of the NFC North and the overall NFC, and where the Lions fall in the clutter.

item.title: NFC South Week 6 Review: There’s finally a team over .500
item.description: Carolina stands alone atop the division, and is threatening to run away with it.
item.content:encoded:
As it often does, the division split wins and losses this week, with the Saints and Panthers coming out on top. The Buccaneers failed to build on last week’s win, and the Falcons are in the midst of their 2nd losing streak of the season. Here’s the Week 6 NFC South Review: 

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5)

Week 6 Result: Buccaneers 19 – Steelers 26
Week 7 Opponent:  Carolina Panthers

Jalon Daniels is fun to watch, mainly because he’s not playing for my team. The UDFA is doing his best, but the limitations are clear, and as Falcons fans can attest, Zac Robinson won’t do much to alleviate them. The Buccaneers had a 13-point lead going into the 4th quarter and squandered it, giving up 16 points and pushing the contest to overtime. Being careless with the football and asking a UDFA to throw the ball 43 times proved to be their undoing.

There’s a chance Baker Mayfield could return soon, but it’s unlikely he’ll mask this team’s issues. Next week they take on the division leaders in Charlotte.

Carolina Panthers (3-2)

Week 6 Result: Panthers 25 – Eagles 14
Week 7 Opponent: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

After a bye week they desperately needed, the Panthers took care of business against a decimated Eagles. Carolina’s offense looks like a well-oiled machine right now. They sit atop the division as the only team in the South above .500. Some might call them “schedule merchants,” but you don’t get to pick the opponents you play, and as every NFL fan has learned, there’s no such thing as easy games in this league.

Carolina can build an even more commanding division lead this weekend when they face the Buccaneers.

New Orleans Saints (2-4)

Week 6 Result: Saints 34 – Giants 27 
Week 7 Opponent: Pittsburgh Steelers

The Saints got a much-needed road win in New York. The offense came alive in the 2nd and 3rd quarters and did just enough to put the game out of reach. JJ McCarthy gave them a scare late in the game, but Kellen Moore’s team was able to survive. Tyler Shough’s all-around play wasn’t that impressive, but he delivered when he absolutely had to. This defense is still one of the worst in the league, but the offense can keep them afloat against most sub-par opponents.

They’ll return to the dome and host the Steelers, who are coming off an overtime win against the Buccaneers. 

Atlanta Falcons (2-4)

Week 6 Result: Falcons 23 – Bears 21
Week 7 Opponent: San Francisco 49ers

The Falcons have lost two games in a row for the second time this season. The offense came out flat, scoring only one touchdown in the first three quarters, and the defense is playing guys at the bottom of the roster across multiple positions. The late effort was good to see, but it was too little too late. This offense struggles under pressure, and it struggles as a unit.

The play calling in these scenarios often relies on long developing routes and lacks quick hitters. Penix is struggling to diagnose pressure and is holding the ball too long, and the offensive line is struggling to win one-on-ones and sort out the blitz. Bijan Robinson also had his worst game as a pass blocker. Things won’t get easier soon, as the team hosts the 49ers and a pair of familiar coaches. 

The Panthers are the only winning team in the division, and if others can’t find their footing soon, it looks like the cats will run away with it. There’s still more than half a season to play, but this could be the least dramatic finish we’ve seen in the NFC South in a long time.

item.title: U2 to perform at halftime on Thanksgiving Eve
item.description: U2 performed a memorable halftime show in New Orleans at Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002 and they will be back on a football field for a brief concert later this year.
item.content:encoded:
U2 performed a memorable halftime show in New Orleans at Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002 and they will be back on a football field for a brief concert later this year.

Netflix announced on Tuesday that the band will perform at halftime of the NFL's first ever Thanksgiving Eve game on November 25. The game will be at SoFi Stadium with the Rams hosting the Packers.

“There's a reason U2 has headlined stadiums for decades: they don't just perform, they deliver iconic moments audiences remember forever," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said in a statement. "We’re thrilled that they'll bring that same magic to the NFL stage on Netflix. It’s going to be an unforgettable night for football fans and Netflix members worldwide.”

Netflix has carried Christmas games the last two seasons and halftime shows for those contests have featured artists like Beyonce and Snoop Dogg, so they may have more to announce ahead of the two games they'll be broadcasting on the holiday this year.

item.title: How long is Terry McLaurin out? Latest updates on Commanders WR's knee injury
item.description: Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin suffered a significant knee injury on "Monday Night Football" vs. 49ers in Week 6. How long will he be out?
item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders lost 23-17 to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 6 on "Monday Night Football", marking their fourth loss of the 2026 NFL season.

That said, Washington's bigger loss was its star wide receiver, Terry McLaurin, who was carted off with a knee injury.

McLaurin was injured in the first quarter and did not return. Now, it looks like he'll miss significant time as a result.

The veteran receiver has already missed one game this year while dealing with a hamstring injury in Week 4. According to the latest reports on Tuesday, Oct. 20, it's possible McLaurin's latest injury is far more severe.

Here's everything to know about McLaurin's knee injury and how long he will be out for the Commanders.

How long is Terry McLaurin out?

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said after the "Monday Night Football" game that the team is concerned McLaurin's injury "could be significant." The veteran wideout will undergo more scans on Tuesday, Oct. 20, Quinn said. Further updates will come when the head coach speaks to the media later in the day on Oct. 20.

"There's fear," Quinn said.

NFL Media and ESPN insider Ian Rapoport reported the morning of Oct. 20 that McLaurin "is feared to have suffered a serious and season-ending knee injury."

What happened to Terry McLaurin?

McLaurin was carted off the field during the Commanders' Week 6 "Monday Night Football" game after suffering a knee injury in the first quarter.

The injury appeared to be non-contact while he was running a route. He got up and walked to the cart with some assistance. His left leg was put in an air cast before teammates surrounded him as he left the game.

Below is a full look at the play that injured McLaurin.

A look at the injury that caused Terry McLaurin to be carted off the field. pic.twitter.com/WhLtj1q67N

— TSN (@TSN_Sports) October 20, 2026

Terry McLaurin injury update

The Commanders quickly ruled out McLaurin with a knee injury.

The team made the decision shortly after the receiver was carted off the field in the first quarter on "Monday Night Football" against the 49ers.

The Commanders did not provide an official status update after the game, but head coach Dan Quinn said the star receiver will undergo further testing.

"The concern is that it could be significant," Quinn said after the game. "We'll do the scans tomorrow and give you an update."

Commanders WR depth chart

Here's a look at the Commanders' current depth chart at wide receiver:

  • Stefon Diggs
  • Antonio Williams
  • Treylon Burks
  • Dyami Brown
  • Luke McCaffrey

Veteran Diggs will step in as Jayden Daniels' top target, with rookie third-round pick Williams set for a bigger role. Burks is likely the biggest beneficiary as the most prominent outside, downfield weapon remaining.
