item.title: Position grades from the Patriots’ win over the Jets
item.description: Our film review of each position group after the Patriots’ 26-19 win over the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
They can’t all be blowouts, can they?

Coming off a convincing 45-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, the New England Patriots found themselves in a much more competitive game versus the New York Jets. A big reason for the game’s comparatively close nature was the Patriots’ own inability to play consistent football between turnovers, dropped passes and uneven run defense.

At the end of the day, they still managed to do enough to secure a 26-19 win and improve to 4-2 on the season. It wasn’t overly pretty, but it was still winning football at the end of the day.

Let’s take a look at the film and hand out some grades.

Patriots film review from NFL Week 6

Quarterback: The typically blitz-heavy Jets decided to alter their approach against Drake Maye, playing a less aggressive form of defense while simultaneously trying to contain him as best they could. They did a solid job, but at the end of the day New England’s quarterback was simply better. Maye delivered some good throws throughout the day, took what the defense gave him, showed some anticipation (see: 3rd-and-10 throw to Kyle Williams), made sound decisions, and once again played at a consistently high level both when throwing the ball and picking his spots to advance it with his legs. His 0.39 expected points added per play are a reflection of that. | Grade: A

Running back: Rhamondre Stevenson averaged only 2.6 yards per carry, but he did what he could: he forced four missed tackles and finished with 36 yards after contact on 36 total rushing yards. He also continued to do some good work as a pass protector, giving up one hurry in 11 reps. TreVeyon Henderson played a limited role after suffering an ankle sprain last week, but he mostly moved well and again showed that he is at his best when operating in space. He did lose a fumble, though, which might have contributed to Corey Kiner seeing some action late. Kiner hit the holes hard and kept the legs churning through contact. | Grade: A-

Wide receiver: The Patriots’ wide receiver group had a rollercoaster day. Romeo Doubs got open for a 42-yard touchdown on the second snap of the day, but suffered a game-ending shoulder injury along the way. DeMario Douglas led the team with seven catches for 86 yards and a touchdown, but he also lost a fumble when somewhat unnecessarily trying to turn a big play into an even bigger one. Kyle Williams caught just one pass, but it was a big one and showed he can do more than just run go routes. Efton Chism played the second-most snaps among the group but did not finish with any catches while also being uneven as a run blocker. And then, there was A.J. Brown. Making his return from a four-week stint on injured reserve, the veteran was rusty particularly as a finisher: he had two drops and multiple other close calls while catching only three passes for 27 yards. On the bright side, he did manage to get open a lot. Drake Maye targeting Brown 10 times was therefore not a case of force-feeding him; throwing to him was the right read more often than not. | Grade: C+

Tight end: Hunter Henry continues to be one of the most reliable players on the Patriots’ roster, especially as a receiver. He showed good wiggle on a 16-yard catch-and-run on the final drive of the first half, and was able to get wide open on his 7-yard touchdown catch. His run blocking was not quite as consistent (one stuff, one penalty). Eli Raridon also had his ups and downs. He did make a nice adjustment on an 11-yard catch in the third quarter, but could have held onto a touchdown in the late second; he also was at the point of attack on a pair of stuffed runs, but performed well as a move blocker. The same is true for Cameron Latu. | Grade: B+

Offensive line: Even though it lost three starters due to injury during the game, the Patriots offensive line generally played at a high level against a defense that had averaged 3.4 sacks per game coming in. Drake Maye was kept clean for much of the day, with the Jets taking him down not even once. Then, late in the game, the unit — using third-string left guard Walter Rouse and fourth-string right guard Matt Pryor — asserted its will in the run game: the group controlled the line of scrimmage, allowing Corey Kiner to keep advancing the ball on eight straight plays. That said, the performance had its moments but was not consistent, especially on the interior. Run blocking was a concern even before the injuries, and both Rouse and center Jared Wilson had a few bad reps between them down the stretch. On the bright side, Will Campbell played some quality football despite nursing a knee injury, while Caleb Lomu mostly performed well after entering for an injured Morgan Moses. With Campbell and Lomu in the fold, the future seems bright at that position for New England. | Grade: B+

Defensive line: The Jets were able to create some movement on the line of scrimmage, and exploit New England’s defense for multiple long runs. Looking at the film, however, it appeared to be less of a performance issue and more of New York doing its homework and being able to use Zak Kuhr’s aggressive approach against him and his defense. There were still problems with misplacement and disengagement, but the Patriots’ talent up front also shone through on multiple occasions. That included Milton Williams and Christian Barmore registering back-to-back sacks — the second featuring a dominant bull-rushing rep from Barmore — while rotational backups Cory Durden, DaQuan Jones and Leonard Taylor had some good moments too. The edge trio of Elijah Ponder, Gabe Jacas and Dre’Mont Jones also continued to be disruptive. Jones was at his best setting an edge in the run game, but was a bit more quiet as a pass rusher. Ponder and Jacas flashed their varied skillsets on multiple reps. | Grade: B

Linebacker: Robert Spillane continues to be the glue that holds the operation together, and one of the most impactful players on the Patriots roster. His run stuff on 4th-and-2 in the early second quarter against a charging Braelon Allen was an impressive display of his ability to hunker down and hold the line. He also was effective as a run blitzer on multiple occasion. He finished the game with three run stuffs, compared to two by his running mate Christian Elliss. They both had missed tackles as well, and also contributed to the Jets finding success with their turning-the-aggressiveness-against-the-defense plan, but on the whole had a quality outing. | Grade: A–

Cornerback: Christian Gonzalez did give up four catches for 45 yards on the day, but only two of those for 20 combined yards came against the Jets’ top receiver. Going up against Garrett Wilson on 17 reps, the Patriots’ No. 1 cornerback more than held his own and forced quarterback Geno Smith to look away from his favorite target repeatedly. Another good outing against a top-tier player. Elsewhere at cornerback, Marcus Jones had a very good day in the office playing both outside and in the slot; he allowed just two passes to be completed to his part of the field. Charles Woods, who again filled in for Carlton Davis as a perimeter corner opposite Gonzalez, looked as good as you would expect a backup to look: there were some hiccups staying with his responsibilities out of bunch formations, but he mostly was well-positioned including on his interception — a play that allowed him to dust off the old receiver skills. | Grade: A

Safety: Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson had some good moments, including an impressive pass breakup by Byard on a throw intended for Mason Taylor. However, there also were some breakdowns — none bigger than Omar Cooper Jr’s 48-yard touchdown in the third quarter. The Patriots used zone on the play, but there appeared to be a miscommunication between the safeties. Woodson rotated down to help defend any crossers in a Cover 3-style assignment, which would have left Byard to defend anything going over the top. However, Byard widened when Cooper charged through them as if playing split-field. Ultimately, neither he nor Woodson were able to make up the ground to defend the play. Byard also missed three tackles on the day, and was flagged for defensive pass interference in the fourth quarter. Woodson was steadier as a whole, but also wasn’t regularly tested deep. | Grade: C

Special teams: Mike Vrabel praised the Patriots’ kickoff unit immediately after the game, and for good reason. The Jets didn’t create much movement running backs kicks, while New England had some good runbacks, especially Corey Kiner’s 37-yarder out to the 40 to set the stage for the time-consuming field goal drive in the late fourth quarter. Marcus Jones gained 10 yards on his lone punt return, while Mitch Wishnowsky’s 54-yard kick in the second quarter was his best since joining the club. The only blemish was Andy Borregales sending an extra point wide to the left early in the fourth quarter, his third total miss this year. | Grade: A–

How would you grade the Patriots’ performance against the Jets? Do you agree with our assessment? Please head down to the comment section to discuss with the rest of the community.

item.title: Martin Emerson Jr. put together statement performance for Saints
item.description: The veteran defensive back delivered his best outing in the black and gold since joining New Orleans this offseason.
item.content:encoded:
Martin Emerson Jr. made his presence felt in the New Orleans Saints’ 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, putting together one of the defense’s most impressive individual performances of the season.

Emerson finished with seven combined tackles, two interceptions, four passes defensed, one pressure and one tackle. His performance earned him an 88.4 overall defensive grade and a 90.2 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus, highlighting just how effective he was against the Giants.

His two interceptions were the biggest difference-makers. Emerson picked off both Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy, and was inches away from a third interception late in the fourth quarter.

For a Saints defense that’s been lacking consistent playmakers in the secondary, Emerson’s performance was exactly the type of showing that can change the conversation surrounding a unit.

The Saints escaped with a seven-point victory after allowing the Giants to erase much of their early deficit. That late-game collapse overshadowed what was otherwise a productive afternoon for several New Orleans players, but Emerson’s performance deserves recognition.

If he can build on this performance, Emerson could become an increasingly important piece of the Saints’ secondary moving forward.

item.title: NFL Week 7 Power Rankings: Teams Trending Up or Down?
item.description: With Week 6 over, @AaronLemingNFL takes a deeper look into each team’s stock watch so far this season in Week 7 WCG Power Rankings
item.content:encoded:
With the conclusion of Week 6, we are inching closer and closer to the midway point of the season. While the league’s elite and bottom-feeders have started to identify themselves, there’s still plenty to be learned in the coming weeks and months about how the NFL’s playoff picture will start to take shape. With six weeks in the books, it’s time to take a stock-watch approach to each team’s season so far and see how it’s trending against preseason expectations—and more in our Week 7 installment of WCG NFL Power Rankings. 

1. San Francisco 49ers (6-0)

Trending: Up

Whew, what a game on Monday night, huh? The only thing stopping some from fully buying into this team is their rash of injuries that just won’t stop. That said, they’ve kept winning, and usually have done so convincingly. This is a very well-rounded team, albeit one of the oldest rosters in the league. With a three-game lead in the division, it’s hard to imagine a scenario where the 49ers aren’t at least in the NFC Championship game, barring a major step back. 

2. Kansas City Chiefs (5-0)

Trending: Up

Six weeks and five games in, it’s safe to say t025 was the outlier and the Chiefs’ window hasn’t closed. While many expected a bounce-back, few saw a perfect 5-0 start coming. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has looked good coming off a torn ACL, and running back Kenneth Walker has been a game-changer. With the Raiders fading and the Broncos’ offensive issues, the AFC West looks like theirs for the taking.

3. Buffalo Bills (5-1)

Trending: Up

It hasn’t always been pretty, and there are still plenty of questions remaining on the defensive side of the ball, but the Bills continue to find ways to win games. Even though the Patriots have rebounded from a slow start, the Bills look like the perennial contender that they are, especially if they can get the defense playing at a higher level. One thing is for sure: having an MVP-caliber quarterback in Josh Allen helps, and he continues to make mind-boggling plays for his team each week. 

4. Minnesota Vikings (5-0)

Trending: Up

No matter how the offense has performed to this point, a 5-0 start is about as much of a dream come true as anything Vikings fans could have asked for. Their defense under Brian Flores continues to play at an elite level. If they can become more productive and consistent offensively, this will be a very dangerous team. Their schedule is about to tighten up, so we’ll see how “for real” their undefeated start proves to be. 

5. New England Patriots (4-2)

Trending: Up

At 1-2 and Drake Maye struggling, it must have felt like the sky was falling in New England. A three-game winning streak later, and the Patriots are just one game out of first place heading into a Thursday night showdown in Chicago. The talent is there, but health has been an issue. We’ll see if they can keep building on their current streak or come back down to earth in the coming weeks. 

6. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2)

Trending: Up

Overall, the Jaguars have been one of the league’s more impressive teams. That said, they tend to play down to their competition, which has led to a few tight games. The talent is there, even if the defense isn’t as good as they showed last year. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has picked up where they left off, but it’s hard not to feel like they blew an opportunity to really run away with the NFC South on Sunday in London. 

7. Green Bay Packers (4-2)

Trending: Up

After a shaky 1-2 start, the Packers have found their stride over the past two weeks, dominating both the Bears and Cowboys at home. Their schedule tightens with matchups against the Lions, Panthers, Patriots, Vikings, and Rams over the next six weeks. If they continue to play as they have, there’s reason to believe they’ll come out of that stretch with a winning record. 

8. Detroit Lions (3-2)

Trending: Up (if they can figure out their defense)

There’s no questioning the offense at this point, but will the return of Brian Branch be enough to get their defense back on the right track? The NFC North is a gauntlet, and Detroit is the only team that hasn’t played a divisional game yet. That changes over the next two weeks with games against the Packers and Vikings. Their matchup against Green Bay will challenge this defense. We’ll see how they respond. 

9. Baltimore Ravens (4-2)

Trending: (Slightly) Up

The Ravens are an odd team to track. On paper, they should be much more dominant than they are, but because of an injury to quarterback Lamar Jackson and their defensive inconsistencies, they’ve produced an up-and-down product so far. On paper, they are the best team in the AFC North. So far, they haven’t consistently played like it. Once Jackson is back, I expect them to round into form. 

10. Chicago Bears (4-2)

Trending: Up (Caleb Williams is back)

Chicago is now 2-1 with Caleb Williams as their starting quarterback, and 2-1 with their backups. Some might look at that as an indictment of Williams, but a deeper dive into the offensive numbers tells a much different story. Assuming he can stay healthy, the primary concern will be the defense. They’ve been about as Jekyll and Hyde as it gets through six weeks. The talent is there, but the consistency has lacked. 

11. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2)

Trending: Up (With some questions)

The defense is clearly improved, and their two losses were against a pair of 4-2 teams. The issue is that their wins have come against teams with a combined 3-14 record. The talent is there, but so far, the weekly consistency hasn’t been. The Bengals remain one of the league’s more intriguing teams. 

12. Seattle Seahawks (3-3)

Trending: Down

Coming into the season, Seattle was one of the more overlooked Super Bowl winners in recent history. Despite a strong start to the season, quarterback Sam Darnold has been turning the ball over at a highly concerning rate. The defense also hasn’t been nearly as dominant. It’s clear they miss running back Kenneth Walker, but the offense needs to figure it out soon if they plan to keep pace with San Francisco in the NFC West. 

13. Denver Broncos (4-2)

Trending: Teetering (without better QB play)

The Broncos were a Bo Nix injury away from making it to the Super Bowl and at least being competitive. That feels weird to say, especially given how this season has started, but the offense has been an issue in almost all six of their games. It starts with quarterback play, but the run game has left a lot to be desired. It’s quite remarkable that they’ve been able to win four games playing like this, but it goes to show just how well-rounded this roster is. If Nix can figure it out, they might ultimately be the favorites in the AFC. 

14. Cleveland Browns (4-2)

Trending: Up (The league’s biggest surprise… So far)

As usual, a few teams are surprises, and a few weeks ago, my vote would have been for the Raiders. That said, the Browns defense has continued to play at a high level without Myles Garrett, and their offense is doing just enough to win them games. No matter how the season ends, sitting at 4-2 and in first place is an outstanding start to the Todd Monken era. 

15. Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2)

Trending: Up (Somehow)

Even without Mike Tomlin, this team feels eerily similar to the last 10 Steelers teams we’ve seen. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers continues to hang around and play well enough, and overall, they are getting enough from their aging roster to have a winning record. That said, I’m just not convinced this lasts over 17 games. We’ll see if they can last. 

16. Carolina Panthers (3-2)

Trending: Up

Is Bryce Young a legitimate MVP candidate? It sure feels like it. In a weak NFC South, the Panthers are set up well to repeat. Really, the biggest question is whether the defense can improve enough to make them real contenders in the NFC playoff picture. Regardless, Young’s growth and overall turnaround over the last two seasons have been nothing short of miraculous. 

17. Las Vegas Raiders (3-3)

Trending: Up (Even after a three-game losing streak)

Even in the most pessimistic view, the Raiders are still well ahead of schedule. Sure, they’ve lost three in a row after opening up 3-0, but two of those losses have been taking legitimate contenders down to the wire. Although Kirk Cousins is playing well, don’t be surprised to see Fernando Mendoza get a shot soon if the losing streak continues. 

18. Los Angeles Rams (2-4)

Trending: Down (Bordering on concerning)

A 2-4 start is concerning enough, but with the Rams’ recent rash of injuries, we must be dangerously close to hitting the panic button. Davante Adams is out for six-to-10 weeks. Poona Ford is gone for the year. Garrett still isn’t back, and now Kobie Turner is lost for the next four-to-six weeks. Considering their struggles already, that’s a lot to overcome, even on the short side of those timelines. A Wild Card spot might be their only hope, and their margin for error is shrinking with each loss. 

19. New York Giants (3-2-1)

Trending: Up (Even if it shouldn’t be)

Have the Giants been surprising, especially in place of Jaxson Dart and his season-ending knee injury? Yes. Are the Giants a good football team? Absolutely not. The good news for them is that the NFC East is a complete dumpster fire, and their fortunate start might be enough to keep them pacing the pack for the remainder of the season. Next up: J.J. McCarthy taking over as the starting quarterback. 

20. Houston Texans (2-4)

Trending: Down (but slowly evening out)

Two weeks ago, the Texans looked down and all but out. Back-to-back wins have brought them back to life, and considering the top-heavy nature of the AFC South, Houston still has an outside shot to get back into the mix for the division. On the plus side, quarterback C.J. Stroud looks like he’s back to his rookie self. Now, if they can get the defense figured out, they can make a run over the final 11 games and make the playoffs yet again. 

21. Atlanta Falcons (2-4)

Trending: Could go either way

Those first two games with Michael Penix felt extremely promising, didn’t they? Their Week 5 loss felt like a touch of bad luck, but Week 6’s home loss to the Bears was much more discouraging. On the plus-side– they are just a game and a half out of first place, but their margin for error shrinks with every loss, even in a bad division. The next few weeks will be very telling for the fate of their season. 

22. Dallas Cowboys (2-4)

Trending: Down

Count me as someone who wasn’t buying this team’s yearly offseason hype. Even with an improved defense on paper, something hasn’t quite passed the smell test with this team in a while, and a lot of it has to do with ownership. Jerry Jones’ continued meddling in the team’s day-to-day activities has to wear on everyone in the building. Right now, this team looks poorly coached and has no answers. The talent is there, and they are in the right division for a slow start, but damn, man.

23. New Orleans Saints (2-4)

Trending: Down (With room to improve)

Some of these statuses will be objective, and this is one for me where I simply expected more. In fact, I picked the Saints to win the South this year, and while that is still possible, there’s been very little to write home about through six weeks. Quarterback Tyler Shough is proving to be worthy enough as a franchise quarterback, but they might still be a year or two away in their rebuilding process. 

24. Indianapolis Colts (2-4)

Trending: Down

General manager Chris Ballard was relieved of his duties on Monday, and barring an unexpected turnaround, head coach Shane Steichen will likely follow him out the door after the season. Simply put, the Colts have been stuck in a similar spot since Ballard took over as GM. Since Andrew Luck retired, they haven’t found a quarterback solution that lasts longer than a year or two. At this point, they should focus on selling off what they can and bracing for a rough 2027 campaign. 

25. New York Jets (2-4)

Trending: Holding Steady

The Jets are a tough team to read. On paper, they’re more talented than last year, and at times, that has shown up on the field. The issue is that they can’t consistently string together good performances, and coaching is still a big question mark. On the plus side, they’ll have three high first-round picks. The bigger issue, at least for the remainder of the season, is how many answers they can find before heading into the offseason. 

26. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5)

Trending: Down (and plummeting)

After handing out contract extensions to both Baker Mayfield and Vita Vea, there’s no way they could have expected this kind of start. To put it bluntly, this has been a team floating in space for long enough, and maybe this was the wake-up call they needed. What’s hard to swallow is that if they could have held onto Sunday’s game against the Steelers, they’d be right in the mix for the division. Instead, they are much closer to challenging for a Top 3 draft pick in April.

27. Philadelphia Eagles (2-4)

Trending: Down (and down bad)

Things were already trending in the wrong direction well before Jalen Hurts’ season-ending blood clot issue, but that feels like the straw that broke the camel’s back. Obviously, the primary (real-world) concern is Hurts’ health, but looking at what this team has done on the field since their unconvincing 2-0 start has been about as bad as it gets. Changes should be coming, and if things keep going downhill, I wouldn’t be surprised if a head-coaching change happens before the conclusion of Week 18. 

28. Washington Commanders (1-4-1)

Trending: Down (But, amazingly, still not out)

I say that as someone who was about to tweet that the team looked like they’d given up on head coach Dan Quinn halfway through Monday night’s game, but then they forced a comeback and almost won. That said, they’ve experienced quite the fall from grace since they made the NFC Championship Game just two seasons ago. Jayden Daniels has looked much better so far this year, but overall, this group lacks a solid core of talent. Even though I don’t expect Quinn to get a third season as head coach, they are still far from out of the NFC East race based on the other three teams ahead of them. 

29. Arizona Cardinals (2-4)

Trending: Holding Steady

Week 1’s win felt like the upset of the year, until it wasn’t. Hell, even their Week 6 win against the Rams felt like a big boost. There’s been a lot of ugly in between, but sometimes we forget in the heat of the moment that some teams were expected to be bad. That’s the Arizona Cardinals, yet they have won two games and have shown some serious growth on defense. The upcoming offseason will be key in getting them back on track for the long haul. 

30. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6)

Trending: Down (Way down)

I’m not sure what the hell happened to the Chargers, but I don’t think anyone who follows the sport would have predicted such a poor start. I know they claim they aren’t ready to sell quite yet, but make no mistake: this team will be sellers once the deadline rolls around in a few weeks. The bigger question is whether or not Jim Harbaugh survives this season. 

31. Tennessee Titans (1-5)

Trending: Down (But they got their first win)

The Robert Saleh-Cam Ward marriage could not be going much worse, but they finally got a much-needed win on Sunday. That said, the issues we’re seeing in Year 2 of Ward’s development were exactly my concern when they hired a defensive-minded head coach to foster his development. The Titans’ record post-Mike Vrabel has been brutal, and I don’t see that changing any time soon. Here’s to hoping they can salvage Ward’s development. 

32. Miami Dolphins (0-5)

Trending: Down (And that’s OK)

The Dolphins are awful, but that was expected. When they cleaned house and hired a new regime from Green Bay, ownership knew this rebuild would be a heavy lift. More importantly, they knew they would need to show patience and let this all play out. Even at 0-5 through six weeks, it’s hard to “hate” the “progress” being made. This is going to be a multi-year effort, but let’s see what things look like after another draft class or two.

item.title: History says Cowboys will be patient with Brian Schottenheimer
item.description: The Cowboys do not have a history of moving on from head coaches before their contracts are up
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys have only two wins through their first six games for just the 16th time in franchise history. Amazingly, and unfortunately, this has now been the case for them in back-to-back seasons.

Brian Schottenheimer’s direct predecessors each oversaw only one start to a season of this variety. For Mike McCarthy (2020), Jason Garrett (2015), and Wade Phillips (2010) mid-October saw them lead the Cowboys to at least a hat trick’s worth of wins more often than not.

Schottenheimer is the subject of great focus for the Cowboys right now and as a result some on the internet are wondering if the Cowboys could look to make a move. You will of course be shocked to learn that the team’s brass said that is in no way on their minds at the moment.

You can file this under “what else are they supposed to say” as the Cowboys know that they are in a bad NFC East and could wind up winning it when this calendar year wraps. Even if that happens, it is hard to see how the critics will cool on Brian Schottenheimer. Winning does cure all, though.

If you are curious what would happen if the wheels continued to fall off, it isn’t exactly the Cowboys’ style to fire coaches midseason. Heck, it isn’t even their style (relative to modern times) to fire them at all.

Wade Phillips was the last head coach who the Cowboys paid to not work for them, and they infamously fired him after a Sunday Night Football loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Sound familiar?

As many have said over the last decade and a half, the Cowboys were clearly comfortable doing that then because they had what they saw to be as an obvious replacement on staff already in Jason Garrett. Garrett did become the next head coach, and he was never fired by the team. The Cowboys saw his contract through twice.

It was after that second one came to an end that Dallas chose to simply not bring him back. They, as you know, brought in Mike McCarthy (who coincidentally delivered the final blow to Wade Phillips that fateful night at Lambeau) and he also saw his contract run through before he and the team went their separate ways. This leads us to our present time.

Schottenheimer signed a four-year deal with the Cowboys when they brought him on in 2025. This means that he isn’t even halfway done which is why the historical context is necessary here. History says the Cowboys will hold.

What do you think, though? Do you think it’s possible this is the time that they buck that trend?

Or do you expect more of the same in that capacity?

item.title: Rams ‘dream season’ being derailed by poor play and injuries
item.description: The injuries pile up for the Los Angeles Rams and more NFL news
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie not to be 2-4 through six weeks, but to compete for a Super Bowl. But the Rams plans have been derailed by poor play, penalties and injuries as the Rams continue to lose key pieces.

Garrett hasn’t suited up since Week 1, McDuffie missed week 6, Davante Adams is hurt, Aaron Donald has missed time, Jaylen Watson has missed time, Puka Nacua has missed time and more.

Alaric Jackson was suspended so we’ll file that one under poor decision making.

Either way, the Rams had a plan, and they are punching themselves in the mouth and need to come up with the new one. I am not saying the season is over, it’s not, but it’s currently being derailed, and it’s up to the Rams to get themselves back on track.

Can they do it? Yes.

Will they do it? We have to keep watching to find out.

Rams star Kobie Turner likely going on IR due to groin injury (ramswire)

“On top of that, star defensive lineman and team captain Kobie Turner will likely have to go on injured reserve, keeping him out of action for the near future. Turner injured his groin and will be out 4-6 weeks, according to Michael J. Duarte of the California Post.

Turner played in only 23 snaps during Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals. That was the second-lowest out of the position group, with Ty Hamilton’s 18 snaps rounding out the count.“

Cardinals Have Sent Rams Into Full-Blown Meltdown After Week 6 Upset (sports.yahoo)

“”Throughout the McVay era, beating the Cardinals was about as ‘sure’ as it gets. This was supposed to be a ‘get right’ game and start a run going into the bye. Instead, they lose 18-16 to a Cardinals team that had waved the white flag on this season,” wrote Rams On SI’s Blaine Grisak.

The national stories aren’t about an incredible achievement from Arizona, who saw Mike LaFleur emerge as the second coach in NFL history to have his first two wins come on the road at the same stadium, but rather about how things are going sideways quickly in Los Angeles:“

Full list of Rams’ terrible injury updates following Week 6 loss (ramswire)

“Davante Adams, Poona Ford, Kobie Turner and Blake Grupe all got injured in the game and will miss extended time, ranging from a few weeks to the rest of the season. When it rains, it pours, and it is torrential in Los Angeles right now.

Here’s a full list of injury updates from McVay following Monday’s press conference.“

Davante Adams set for lengthy layoff as LA Rams rocked by injury blows (aol.com)

“In his 13th NFL campaign, the 33-year-old wide receiver has recorded 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns this year. Adams previously missed three late-season contests with a hamstring issue last year before coming back for postseason play.

“It’s significant when you don’t have a player like Davante, but we have to be able to adjust,” McVay said. “His contributions can’t be measured. You don’t replace somebody like him, and so what you’ve got to do is you’ve got to be able to figure out what’s the next right thing? What does that look like in terms of our vision? We’ll have to adjust and adapt.”

NFC West update: LA Rams in injury crisis mode with several long-term absences (fieldgulls)

“It bodes well for Seattle, who—like Los Angeles have dropped back-to-back games and have looked like a shell of themselves as of late. However, it certainly helps one of the most dangerous forces in the NFC has as well.

Despite the injury news, the Rams are set to take on the Las Vegas Raiders, Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders and the Cardinals over their next four games—a favourable upcoming stretch of games by all means.

Given the star power on their roster, it’s difficult to count Los Angeles out of the playoff picture, even nearing the halfway mark of the season, but there’s certainly work to be done if they want to keep up in the NFC race.“

What has gone wrong for the 2-4 Rams after ‘superteam’ hype? Can they fix it? (espn.com)

“Well, the alarms are now going off in Los Angeles. On Sunday, the Rams lost 18-16 at home to a 1-4 Cardinals team, the sort of defeat that inspires soul searching and painful self-reflection. Any team can lose when the turnovers don’t bounce its way or an injury unexpectedly costs it a key player, but neither of those were the case against Arizona. And while the Rams lost new kicker Blake Grupe to an early-game knee injury, special teams weren’t really to blame for the loss, either.

Are the 2-4 Rams, who were the prohibitive favorites to win the Super Bowl after acquiring Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie and bringing Aaron Donald out of retirement this offseason, just not very good? Do we know enough after six games to say with confidence that the superteam Rams we expected to see heading into the season aren’t ever going to show up on the field in 2026? Is it time to write them off as Super Bowl contenders?

One thing I can say for sure: To live up to the preseason hype and win the Super Bowl, the Rams will have to do something no NFL team has ever done before. If the Rams even make it to the Super Bowl, they would be the first team in NFL history to post a losing record through six weeks and still manage to win its conference in the Super Bowl era. Playing in an era with a 17-game regular season and 14 playoff teams makes a potential turnaround a little easier for the Rams, but they would have to break 60 years of precedent to overcome this slow start.“

3 takeaways from Rams’ rash of major injuries suffered in Week 6 (ramswire)

“With all their losses, here are three takeaways on what they mean for the Rams.

Nacua needs to be at his absolute best

Puka Nacua will be called upon even more with Adams being out for an estimated 6-10 weeks. In the last year of his deal, Nacua has found his form in recent weeks and is making the ultimate push to become the NFL’s highest-paid non-quarterback.“

Legendary band to play Rams-Packers halftime show on Thanksgiving Eve (sports.yahoo)

“Netflix announced on Tuesday that legendary rock band U2 will play the halftime show during the Los Angeles Rams‘ game against the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. That game takes place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, bringing the iconic band to the Rams’ house for a special performance.

It’s the NFL’s first game ever on Thanksgiving Eve, and it comes after the Rams’ Week 11 bye. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. ET and will be streamed live on Netflix, just as the Rams’ season opener against the 49ers was.

U2, led by Bono and The Edge, have won 22 Grammy Awards, including Best Album for The Joshua Tree in 1987.“

Rams’ devasting wave of Week 6 injuries might be the final blow (ramblinfan)

“Defensive tackle Kobie Turner: groin injury. Out four to six weeks, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter.

Kicker Blake Grupe: torn ACL. Done for the year. 

That’s on top of existing injuries to star cornerback Trent McDuffie, who missed the game against Arizona and is in question for Week 7. Myles Garrett, McVay said, will not return to practice this week. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year has been on injured reserve since Week 1. The Horns’ season from hell is here.

What’s next for the Rams after losing multiple stars

Where does the team go from here? First things first, they’ll have to sign a kicker. McVay expects that to happen in the next day or two. “

Commanders-49ers on ‘Monday Night Football’: What We Learned from San Francisco’s 23-17 win (nfl.com)

“Niners survive second-half hibernation. Monday night’s showdown started off lopsided just as many prognosticated. The 49ers made Odyssey-length marches look commonplace, going 64 yards or longer on four of their first five possessions and turning them into 20 points. Brock Purdy started off on fire, throwing numerous pinpoint passes and twice extending drives by scrambling to move the chains on third down or later. Christian McCaffrey scored twice, running his touchdown streak to five games, while George Kittle collected five catches for 69 yards and his fifth TD of the young season. The 49ers totaled 303 yards to Washington’s 90 at halftime, with a 20-3 lead they extended to 23-3 with a 65-yard drive for a field goal on their first possession of the third quarter. Then came the comeback. While Washington deserves a lot of the credit, the 49ers’ offensive problems can be traced back to Mike Evans going down with an Achilles injury with 1:03 remaining in the second quarter. San Francisco was able to travel another 12 yards to finish it off with a score, and the offense had the aforementioned 65-yard trek without him on its only drive of the third quarter. However, the 49ers went three-and-out on three fourth-quarter possessions to let the Commanders back in it. Evans finished the game with a team-leading 94 receiving yards. Kittle and McCaffrey had a combined 18 targets, while no other Niners pass catcher saw more than two. There was no one else healthy left to throw to, and it would’ve cost the 49ers had their defense not saved the day with two massive stops at the end of the game. Evans has been on a lot of injury reports all season, but he’s made every start. He’s clearly vital to the operation. Luckily, head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that Evans is only sore and won’t require more testing. That’s major for a Niners wide receiver room that has sustained heavy losses.“

Comment of the day:

“2-4 with a remaining schedule that includes; KC, Packers, SF and Seattle x2. I watched LV today. They ain’t that bad. If we can’t beat the Cards at home, who can we beat? What’re we shooting for max now 9-8 or 8-9, maybe? Won’t be good enough to make the playoffs. IM

iMO this season went down the drain because of the below reasons;

  1. Bad drafting in ‘24, 25 and ‘26. None of the draftees have lived up to expectations. Neither Verse, nor Fiske could ever close the deal on actual tackles and sacks. Ferguson has had little to no positive impact at TE. Then we drafted three guys who would never contribute as rookies including another TE.
  2. the Myles Garrett trade and associated media hype.
  3. the distraction of being on the fence so long about the return of Aaron Donald. Had we not acquired Garrett, Donald would’ve stayed retired and not damaged his legacy.
  4. Not addressing lack of talent in our starting crew of UDFA LB’s.
  5. Not addressing the League’s worst Special Teams crew.
  6. Not getting a credible #3 WR.
  7. The League, especially the NFC West, has solved the mystery of the McVay offensive schemes.
  8. Shula is a lousy DC.
  9. We have been victimized by some of the worst officiating I’ve seen in over 5 decades.
  10. This overall team is lackadaisical. There’s no chemistry, fire in the belly or force of will to put away and soundly defeat other teams.

*something bad happened to this team after the late 2025 regular season loss to Carolina. We then proceeded to lose a game we led 30-14 late at Seattle that cost us the NFC West title and then there was that final inexplicable loss at Atlanta. In the playoffs, we barely squeaked by a weak Carolina team in the last minute. I was there. Then we had to go to OT to beat a questionably good Chicago team. Finally, we lost a close one at Seattle when we couldn’t stop Cooper Kupp from converting a 3rd and long in the NFC Championship with the clock running out. It seems that we really haven’t played good fb since that November 30th loss to the Panthers. 🤔“ -SlowTightEnd

item.title: Browns offense still needs a spark, but these two players stepped up against Ravens
item.description: The Browns got big days from Jaleel McLaughlin and Jerry Jeudy.
item.content:encoded:
There’s something about the Browns’ offense in the second half that gets clicking. 237 yards of offense on the day doesn’t sound too impressive, but take into consideration that they only had 46 yards of offense in the first half. Ultimately, they actually out-gained the Ravens, thanks to a strong defensive performance. The team playing complete football (i.e. sticking with things to the end) has worked for four close victories, but to take the next step, they have to obviously break out of that trend to the upside.

Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns’ Week 6 game against the Baltimore Ravens.

Quarterback

  • It’s tough to say whether things are processing slower for Deshaun Watson, or if players simply weren’t getting open and he doesn’t want to force the turnover because of that. The announcers kept calling out that players weren’t open, and the few replays that they showed were indicating that as well.
  • I think it’s a mixture of both. I don’t see panic from Watson, but at times, he takes off with what looks to be a decent opening to get some positive yardage. That has worked against some teams, but against the Ravens, their defensive front seemed quicker to close the gap and prevent him from escaping. So if that’s the case against a certain defense, Watson has to discover that balance of perhaps hanging in an extra tick and delivering the ball somewhere.
  • I feel like part of the problem was the gameplan to try pushing the ball downfield too much early. Watson has been at his most efficient when he mixes in short read passes through his progressions with the intermediate throws, which we saw him get back to in the second half. PFF graded Watson out to a 56.4 on the day.

Running Back

  • It was a solid running day for Jaleel McLaughlin, who offers that ability to shift his way through a small gap. Again, it wasn’t anything crazy, but it was something that made me feel like we have a chance on squeezing some extra yards out via the ground. I feel like Quinshon Judkins would’ve been stuck in that 3.0 YPC territory on those same plays, based on how he’s played this year. McLaughlin was the Browns’ second-highest graded player on offense, grading out to a 76.6.
  • Audric Estime, just signed, got the team’s lone touchdown of the day down at the goal line.
  • Fullback Michael Burton got his first touch of the season, moving the chains on a fourth down play off of a fullback handoff.

Wide Receiver

  • Welcome back, Jerry Jeudy, He secured the passes thrown to him well, and they all seemed to come at big moments. His snap count usage ticked up a hair from two weeks ago, and he was the Browns’ top-graded receiver this week by PFF, with a grade of 76.1.
  • KC Concepcion also had a big catch late off of a short laser. I liked trying to incorporate him on a jet sweep, but the defensive back played it well. Cleveland was also going to try a trick play with him throwing the ball, but he wisely aborted the play when it was covered.
  • It was the first game where Denzel Boston was a relative non-factor, although Watson did try to loft a touchdown pass to him in the fourth quarter (but it was out of bounds).

Tight End

  • Not much action for the tight ends again this week. After a relatively hot start for Harold Fannin, it seems unusual to not have him targeted or involved much the past two weeks offensively, despite all the snaps he plays. He ended up being the lowest-graded player on offense by PFF, grading out to a 51.6.

Offensive Line

  • The offensive line was healthy and played the whole game.
  • Cleveland allowed 5 sacks on the day, but PFF only charged one of those to the offensive line (being on C Elgton Jenkins).
  • The Browns’ top-graded player on offense this week? Left guard Zion Johnson, although it was mostly for his run-blocking grade, as his pass blocking grade was below everybody else. Tytus Howard and Austin Barber also received solid grades for their job against the Ravens.

item.title: John Harbaugh on RB timeshare: Someone has to "do something" to earn job
item.description: Giants running backs ran 14 times for 34 yards in last Sunday's loss to the Saints and one of their backs said after the game that he thinks the rotation of backs is working against the team.
item.content:encoded:
Giants running backs ran 14 times for 34 yards in last Sunday's loss to the Saints and one of their backs said after the game that he thinks the rotation of backs is working against the team.

Najee Harris and Devin Singletary had four carries in the game, Tyrone Tracy had six and Cam Skattebo didn't touch the ball at all after leading the team in carries through the first five weeks of the season. Harris said, via Greg Johnson of the Trentonian, that it is "hard to get into a rhythm" while constantly going in and out of the game and those comments were brought up to head coach John Harbaugh during Monday's press conference.

Harbaugh said he understands that feeling, but said that the opportunity to develop that kind of rhythm is something that has to be earned and no one has done that to this point.

"I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven't. Our run game hasn't earned that yet, and none of those guys have. My advice would be to any player, and it's all the guys, we had the same conversation. I've had the same conversation with all the running backs, the receivers, it's no different than any position, but do the most you can with the opportunities you get. Make the most of those opportunities and you're sure to get more opportunities. Do something."

The Giants made the choice to move on from Barkley before Harbaugh was in the organization, but invoking Henry is interesting because he and the Ravens were criticized in Week 16 last season for pulling Henry in favor of Keaton Mitchell at key moments in the second half against the Patriots. New England came back from 11 points down in the fourth quarter for a 28-24 win that helped keep the Ravens out of the playoffs and contributed to Harbaugh being fired at the end of the season.

No one would argue that any of the Giants backs are in Henry's class, but history says that the division of labor might not be any more ideal if that was the case.

item.title: Film study: Packers’ deep passing attack is a paper tiger
item.description: The Packers’ deep passing game has situational tendencies the Lions can exploit in their Week 7 divisional matchup
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions (3-2) will take on their first divisional opponent in Week 7 as the Green Bay Packers (4-2) come to Ford Field Sunday afternoon fresh off two big wins.

Let’s just get straight to the point and talk about the elephant in the room. All eyes will be on the Lions defense—and particularly the secondary—as it takes on the Packers’ passing attack. Headed into Week 6, the Packers boasted the fourth-highest explosive play rate in passing offense while the Lions defense checked in at 17th, despite giving up a league-high 297.4 passing yards per game.

The mission of this film study is to generate a scouting report aimed at diagnosing what patterns and tendencies, if any, the Packers have shown in their deep passing game and what that means for the Lions defense.

So I watched all 32 of the Packers’ pass attempts of 20+ air yards and came away with some interesting insights.

Packers’ aggression comes overwhelmingly in comfortable game scripts

The first and most critical tendency to take note of is that, per NFL Pro, of the 32 passes of 20+ air yards or more attempted this season, only four have come while trailing their opponent. In fact, all four of these passes came in a single game: Week 3 against the Atlanta Falcons. Digging even deeper, two of the four occurred after the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter, when the Packers were down by a score of 35-14. Further, all four pass attempts were incomplete.

Okay, but surely this could be misleading, and the Packers have just played with either a tie or lead in many games, much like we say on “Sunday Night Football” against the Dallas Cowboys?

Not really. Quarterback Jordan Love has attempted 60 passes this season while the team has been behind in score. I’ll do the math for you. That is only a 6.67% deep pass rate while trailing. Compare that to 16 deep passes attempted while the Packers are playing with the lead on 103 total passing attempts with a lead. That’s 15.5%.

Okay, but surely this is just a small sample size trend, right?

Not really. To further magnify the situational shift in play calling, the Packers have attempted short passes of under 10 air yards 64 times on 103 pass plays (62.2%) with the lead compared to 44 times on 60 pass plays (73.3%) while trailing.

Head coach Matt LaFleur clearly has a tendency toward paradoxical aggression. He tends to take risks when he’s living in advantageous game scripts, but his focus shifts to a low-risk approach when the game script pressure turns up. This creates a perception of the deep passing game being a strength, but the reality is it’s more of a “kill shot” tool, and when it rains, it pours.

Compare that to Lions offensive coordinator and Drew Petzing and Jared Goff, who have executed the same number of deep passes of 20+ air yards or more (6) when trailing in score as when leading in score, showing no situational tendency so far in 2026’s early sample size.

For the Lions to avoid falling victim in the explosive passing game, the key to winning here is to score early and play with a lead.

Packers’ aggression comes overwhelmingly in certain down-and-distances

The second critical tendency to take note of is that, per NFL Pro, the Packers rarely throw the deep ball in short-to-medium yards-to-go situations, especially on second down.

Of the 32 passes of 20+ air yards or more, they break down in the following downs and distances:

  • first-and-10 (11)
  • third-and-long (7+ yards) (9)
  • second-and-long (7+ yards) (6)
  • third-and-medium/short (0-6 yards) (4)
  • second-and-medium (4-6 yards) (2)
  • second-and-short (0-3 yards) (0)

The key insight here is that LaFleur’s play calling tends not to take advantage of “waste” downs, which I would categorize as the second-and-short/medium range to take shots down the field. Of the two deep passes noted in second-and-medium situations, both were against Dallas in Week 6 and were second-and-6s from inside the Dallas 26-yard line.

It is interesting that LaFleur likes to take risks predominantly with the lead, but does not feel comfortable taking the same risks in advantageous down-and-distance situations.

Packers’ deep ball success is feast or famine

The third critical insight in the Packers’ deep passing game is that its success is remarkably feast or famine. Overall, Jordan Love has completed 10-of-32 (31%) deep passes of 20+ air yards. But six of those 10 completions came in a single game: Week 5 against the Chicago Bears, where Love went 6-for-8 on deep passes. In three games, Love did not complete a single deep pass (0-for-3 vs the New York Jets, 0-for-7 vs the Atlanta Falcons, and 0-for-6 vs the Dallas Cowboys).

Without the Week 5 explosion week, the Packers are just 4-for-26 (15.8%) on deep passes on the season. So what happened against the Bears?

Five of the eight deep passes against Chicago came on first-and-10 situations, four of which were play-action passes.

Below is the first. This is a simple two-man fade-out combination route. If the quarterback sees Cover-3, the out is opened under the outside fade. But in this case, the Bears are in Cover-2, where the deep, field-side safety is responsible for the outside fade. The Bears safety is caught with dirty eyes in the backfield and flat-footed, a huge missed execution play leading to the Green Bay touchdown that should not have been so easy. If the Lions rookie Keith Abney gets more snaps at the free safety spot this week, expect the Packers to test his eyes.

A key point in the above clip is that the play design is also a simple single read for Jordan Love. On the two-man route concept, it’s not a strenuous progression with both routes to the same side of the field.

Similarly, below is another simple single read concept with the core routes all to the field-side of the formation. LaFleur is not asking a lot of Love with either of these concepts. To his credit, Love executes this with great timing and ball placement before Bears’ rookie safety Dillon Theineman (31) can close the gap in the zone.

Overall thoughts

The Lions’ passing defense has not been great against deep passes this year, giving up 12 completions on 22 attempts. But outside of the Bears game, the Packers are not an unstoppable force in this area either.

In addition to the tendencies discussed already, it’s clear that Love has his favorites, with 14-of-32 deep targets going to Matthew Golden and 10-of-32 going to Christian Watson. It will be interesting to see if defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deploys any similarly unique coverages against the Packers as he did against the Arizona Cardinals.

Lastly, Love does not seem to be impacted one way or the other when it comes to handling pressure in his deep passing ability, as he is 4-of-16 while under pressure and 6-of-16 while kept clean.

Score early. Play with a lead. Don’t play with dirty eyes.

item.title: Getting Defensive: Week 7 fantasy plays led by Vikings, Steelers; top streaming defenses
item.description: Gary Davenport breaks down the fantasy football defense landscape headed into Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
For most fantasy managers who paid up for a so-called “elite” fantasy defense over the summer, through six weeks things have been…not great.

In terms of Average Draft Position, the first three defenses drafted this year were the Houston Texans, Los Angeles Rams and Denver Broncos. The Texans have a loaded unit filled with high-end talent at all three levels. The Rams added the reigning Defensive Player of the Year in an offseason trade and got defensive tackle Aaron Donald back. The Broncos led the league in sacks last year.

Well, you see, what had happened was…

The Texans started the season 0-4 in large part because their supposedly loaded defense has been decidedly mediocre most of the season. The Rams are also 2-4 and got all of one game out of Myles Garrett before he landed on injured reserve. Six weeks into the season, both teams rank outside the top-20 defenses in fantasy points.

The Broncos got off to a bumpy start, too. Two weeks into the season, Denver was ranked outside the top-20, too. But Denver has rebounded with three big outings in four weeks, including five sacks and three takeaways last week against the Seattle Seahawks, the Broncos enter Week 7 third at the position in fantasy points.

There’s still a lot of season to go, but consider this a friendly October reminder to file away for next summer.

Don’t pay retail for defenses in drafts.

Just don’t.

Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Week 7: Omar Cooper Jr. and Germie Bernard break out
Germie Bernard and Omar Cooper Jr. are coming online just in time to save fantasy football teams. They headline the biggest names on the Week 7 waiver wire.
  • Kyle Dvorchak,

THE NO-DOUBTERS

Minnesota Vikings (vs. Indianapolis Colts)

Despite playing one less game than most teams, the Vikings remain fantasy football’s No. 1 defense—in the admittedly generic scoring I use for this column (cast a wide net), the Vikes are more than three points per game past every other team. Now, Brian Flores’ ultra-aggressive squad takes on an Indianapolis Colts team that just lost at home to the winless Tennessee Titans. The Colts don’t have the speed to make Minnesota back their safeties off. It’s going to be all stacked fronts, blitzes and anaconda meets capybara.

Pittsburgh Steelers (vs. New Orleans Saints—Paris)

The Steelers are the AFC contender no one wants to call a contender despite their 4-2 start, and edge-rusher T.J. Watt and the defense are a big reason why—the latest iteration of “The Steel Curtain” has more fantasy points than any defense in the AFC after logging five sacks and a pair of takeaways in last week’s overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Saints have moved the ball at times this year and overseas games can get weird, but New Orleans is also third in the league in giveaways this year.

Denver Broncos (at Arizona Cardinals)

As was mentioned in this week’s thrilling, informative and entertaining intro (just how this writer rolls), the Broncos have been rolling the past month—Denver has the No. 1 fantasy defense over the last four weeks. The Cardinals have some weapons on offense and have been a below-average matchup for defenses in fantasy, but if you can heat Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett up the Arizona offense becomes very hit-or-miss. The Broncos will do so and move to 5-2, despite having an offense that is quite offensive—to offense.

San Francisco 49ers (at Atlanta Falcons)

The 49ers are like Thanos—they are inevitable. Six weeks in, the 49ers sit fourth in the NFL in total defense and seventh in the NFL against the pass, while allowing 18.6 points per game—second-fewest in the NFC. The 49ers haven’t pressured opposing quarterbacks consistently, but San Francisco is still second among fantasy defenses over the last three weeks headed into a favorable matchup with a Falcons team giving up the third-most fantasy points per game to defenses this season.

Cleveland Browns (at Tennessee Titans)

Raise you hand if you thought that the Browns would be the clear winners of the Myles Garrett trade six weeks into the season. Now put your hand down—lying is wrong. The Browns have taken a step back from last year’s squad, but it’s a baby step—the Browns are ninth in the league against the pass, seventh in points allowed and have surrendered less than 20 points just twice in six games. Meanwhile, the Titans have scored more than 20 points once this season—last week against the Colts.

Kansas City Chiefs (at Seattle Seahawks)

Steve Spagnuolo’s defense has long been overshadowed by Patrick Mahomes and the offense in Kansas City. But it has played a sizable role in the team’s 5-0 start—the Chiefs are eighth in total defense, sixth against the run and lead the AFC in scoring defense at 16.6 points per game. Taking on the reigning Super Bowl champions in Seattle is no joke, but the past few weeks Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has looked rough—no NFC team has allowed more fantasy points per game to defenses over the past two weeks.

Fantasy Football Kicker Streamers: The 3 best pickups for Week 7
Denny Carter looks into which kickers have the best matchups headed into Week 7.
  • Denny Carter,

STREAMERS OF THE WORLD, UNITE!

Houston Texans (vs. New York Giants)

Yep. This is where we’re at with the Texans—Houston has legitimately had one decent defensive effort in six games this year, and it wasn’t last week in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars. But the Texans are in desperation-mode at home against the Giants this week, New York has major questions at quarterback and running back and the G-Men have allowed the eighth-most fantasy points per game to opposing defenses this year. This week at least, the Texans will look like we thought they would this season.

New York Jets (at Miami Dolphins)

In many respects, this year’s New York Jets team looks a lot last year’s Jets team—in that the losses are piling up again. But the Jets defense has quietly kept the team in games—New York ranks just outside the top-10 in yards allowed per game and possess a top-10 scoring defense, allowing just 20.3 yards per game. At the risk of being accused of October hyperbole, New York’s trip south is a must-win game—and the Dolphins have given up the fourth-most fantasy points per game to defenses this year.

Carolina Panthers (vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

The Carolina Panthers are in first place in the NFC South and have a top-15 fantasy defense, but the latter is an even bigger mirage than the former—the Panthers are 26th in the league in total defense and most of their fantasy scoring came against a rookie third-string quarterback in Week 2. But six weeks into the 2026 season, there isn’t a team in the league giving up more fantasy points per game to defenses than the Buccaneers, and it’s going to take more than Baker Mayfield’s potential return to change that.

Tennessee Titans (vs. Cleveland Browns)

In this week’s edition of scraping the bottom of the D/ST barrel, we have the suddenly resurgent Tennessee Titans, who just got the Colts’ general manager fired. The Titans were Week 6’s highest scoring defense because nothing matters anymore, logging six sacks, three takeaways and a defensive score. Are the Titans going to do that again? Probably not. But the Browns have allowed a league-high 24 sacks and the sixth-most fantasy points to defenses this season. Just saying.

CAVEAT EMPTOR, FOLKS!

Seattle Seahawks (vs. Kansas City Chiefs)

The Seahawks are doing some soul-searching after losing three of their last four games, but the team’s “Dark Side” defense has been solid for fantasy managers—the team is a top-five fantasy defense six weeks into the season. But Seattle’s offense hasn’t been doing the defense any favors over the past month, and this week’s matchup with the Chiefs is nightmare fuel—Kansas City is playing as well as any team in the league offensively, and no squad in the AFC has given up fewer fantasy points per game to defenses this year.

In a 34-31 win over the Jaguars, Noel did not start. He recorded four receptions for a career high 107 yards, a receiving touchdown, one punt return for two yards and returned two kickoffs for 65 yards. Noel recorded 31 offensive snaps and six on special teams.
