item.title: Aaron Glenn: Frank Reich is doing a good job as offensive coordinator
item.description: The Jets finished 29th in points scored during Aaron Glenn's first season as their head coach, so it was not a great surprise that they made the choice to fire offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand at the end of the campaign.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets finished 29th in points scored during Aaron Glenn's first season as their head coach, so it was not a great surprise that they made the choice to fire offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand at the end of the campaign.

Frank Reich was the choice to replace him and the Jets acquired quarterback Geno Smith while making other changes to the unit, but the results have not been much different through six games. They are 27th in points scored, dead last in red zone efficiency and in the bottom portion of the league in a number of other metrics. It hasn't helped

Their Week 6 loss to the Patriots turned in part on a pair of failed fourth down conversions that saw the Jets get stopped short on a pair of runs, which is also something that contributed to their loss to the Packers in Week 2. On Monday, Glenn was asked if he's happy with what he's seen from Reich thus far.

"I think he's done a good job. I really do," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "Obviously, there are a number of things that we can improve on, and I think I just told you guys that from short yards to two-minute, but that also goes on me also when it comes to the defensive side, me and [defensive coordinator Brian] Duker on some things that we have to get better at, too. We have to improve on some things and that's what the season is. That's what practice is. After six games, it's hard to just say, 'Okay we're this.' We have to see how this thing plays out, but I would say I think he's done a good job. . . . As we continue to go through this season, I'll continue to see us progress and getter better on the things we have to get better at. To answer your question, I think he's done a good job."

Injuries have kept running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell off the field in recent games while first-round pick Omar Cooper just got back on the field after a Week 1 ankle injury. Cooper had a strong game against the Patriots, which was a promising development for what Reich could do with a full hand but more tangible results will have to come one way or another for the Jets to improve on a 2-4 start.

item.title: Romeo Doubs injury reportedly not considered a ‘long-term’ issue
item.description: The wide receiver was placed on injured reserve on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Amid a series of roster moves on Monday, the New England Patriots also decided to place wide receiver Romeo Doubs on injured reserve. As a consequence, the offseason signing will be out for at least the next four games.

The absence being much longer than that, however, is not expected. According to a report by Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, Doubs is “hopeful to return after the Week 11 bye” and that the current belief is that his stint on IR will not be a “long-term” affair.

Doubs, 26, hurt his shoulder during the Patriots’ 26-19 win over the New York Jets on Sunday. He came down hard after catching a 42-yard touchdown on his team’s second offensive snap of the day, and subsequently exited the contest. Initially deemed questionable to return, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game at the start of the third quarter.

On Monday, he was sent to injured reserve. Per NFL rules, Doubs will therefore not be eligible to start practicing until after New England’s Week 10 game versus the Detroit Lions.

The timing is favorable for player and club alike, though. With the Patriots on a bye coming out of their cross-Atlantic trip to play the Lions in Germany, Doubs will have an extra week to get up to speed before his team’s next game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12.

With Doubs on IR, the Patriots have four receivers remaining on their active roster. A.J. Brown, who himself returned from an ankle injury just last week and made his comeback against the Jets, as well as DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism. Mack Hollins, who has been on injured reserve since Week 5 with a calf issue, will be eligible to return to practice and the 53-man team in Week 9.

The Patriots will travel to Chicago this week to face the Bears on Thursday Night Football.

item.title: Browns upcoming schedule before Thanksgiving, including bye week, trade deadline
item.description: Cleveland Browns schedule is an interesting one starting with 3 straight road games before the trade deadline, bye week
item.content:encoded:
As much as the NFL dominates the sports calendar, it is the shortest season of the three historically major sports in the United States. It seems like just yesterday the Cleveland Browns were setting their initial 53-man roster and getting ready for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.

The Browns are now six games into their season, have crossed the quarter pole of the year a couple of weeks ago, and have two other schedule markers just ahead: The NFL trade deadline and their bye week.

Could GM Andrew Berry be big game hunting at the deadline, with the potential of a very high pick coming from the Los Angeles Rams due to injury? Will the roster be resting up for a late playoff push? Will fans, and Cleveland natives like Jason Kelce, have the Browns on their minds at Thanksgiving with family?

Here is Cleveland’s schedule, including the deadline and bye week, heading into Turkey Day:

  • 10/25: Away versus the Tennessee Titans
  • 11/1: Away versus the Pittsburgh Steelers
  • 11/8: Away versus the New Orleans Saints
  • 11/10: NFL trade deadline at 4 PM Eastern
  • 11/15: At home versus the Houston Texans
  • 11/22: Bye Week
  • 11/26: Thanksgiving Day

A lot to happen between the end of Week 6 and Thanksgiving, especially with three straight road games. The positives are facing the one-win Titans, the Steelers the week after they return from the first game in Paris (amid civil unrest happening in France), and a Saints team that has seen QB Tyler Shough come back to earth pretty quickly.

Winning two or all of their next three games could give Berry even more confidence to be aggressive at the deadline. The bye week happening later in the season could give the young Browns roster a chance to recover and any new additions more time to get acclimated to the team.

If all that happens, Cleveland fans will be stuffing their faces with good food on Thanksgiving while opening their mouths to talk nothing but the Browns.

I believe the young folk call that “wishcasting.”
